 Mumbai: A sharp sell-off engulfed Indian equities on Thursday, with the Sensex and Nifty dropping over 1.4% each to their 2026 lows as the prospect of higher interest rates , elevated crude prices and continued weakness in the rupee further fuelled risk-off sentiment.
 The BSE Sensex fell 1,045.46 points or 1.44% to close at 71,593.24-the lowest closing since February 2024.
The Nifty declined 371.25 points or 1.64% to close at 22,231.80-the lowest closing since April 2025.
The fall wiped out around ₹10 lakh crore from the market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies.
Adani Enterprises fell 5.4%, while JSW Steel and ITC dropped 4.5% and 4%, respectively.
 Live Events
India's Volatility Index or VIX, the street's fear gauge, shot up by 10.26% in response to the uncertainty. Elsewhere in Asia, China sank 0.8%, Hong Kong fell 1.4%, South Korea declined 2.7% and Taiwan dropped 0.9%. The pan-Europe index Stoxx 600 was down 0.3% at the time of going to print. Jitters over the outlook on India have been elevated of late on account of a number of factors, but higher oil prices and global central banks signalling further interest rate increases are bothering investors the most.
"The market is witnessing a barrage of bad news-rising rates globally, weakening rupee, triple-digit oil prices, IPO supply, political protests, supply chain disruptions, below-average monsoon, lack of AI opportunities and FPI selling," said Nilesh Shah, MD, Kotak Mahindra Asset Management Co.
 Read more: Market Trading Guide: Deepa Jewellers among 2 stock recommendations for Friday 
After Thursday's fall, the Sensex has slid nearly 16% and the Nifty has dropped 15% so far in 2026, resulting in Indian stocks emerging as among the worst performers globally.
On Thursday, the Nifty Midcap 150 and the Nifty Small-cap 250 dropped 2.4% each.
 Read more: RBI rate hike done. Now what’s ahead for bank stocks? Jefferies, other brokerages weigh in 
Of the 4,654 shares traded on the BSE, 3,545 declined, while 910 advanced.
So far in 2026, the Nifty Midcap 150 is down 4.3%. The Nifty Smallcap 250 is up 4.8%.
Brent crude surged 4.1% to above $104 a barrel on Thursday, due to renewed worries about the lingering West Asia conflict.

docs.title: TCS Q2 profit rises 15% to Rs 13,884 crore as AI revenue doubles; growth remains subdued
docs.text:
Bengaluru: Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), India's largest software services firm, posted a 15% rise in net profit to ₹13,884 crore in the September quarter from a year ago while revenue rose 11.2% to ₹73,188 crore, largely in line with analyst estimates. The numbers were buoyed by growth returning in a small way, especially in the largest segment of banking and financial services along with AI services, which crossed $3.1 billion on an annualised basis, accounting for about 10% of total revenue.
 On a sequential basis, profit was up 4% while revenue gained a modest 1.26%. On a constant currency basis, growth was largely flat at 0.5%. This was the slowest growth in three years in the second quarter, which is a seasonally strong one.
Operating margin narrowed 120 basis points to 24% due to the impact of higher operating expenses as hiring rebounded slightly with TCS onboarding 4,258 people. 
Chief executive K Krithivasan said he was "positive" medium-term growth should recover going by the total contract value and the conversations that the company is having with the clients. "We are pleased with broad-based growth in all our international markets and most industry segments," he said on an analyst call.
The $300-billion Indian IT industry has been reeling under the impact of weak spending on technology due to global uncertainty and disruptions, along with the impact of AI-led automation eating into the earnings of companies.
 Live Events
"This quarter we announced two unique deals with Porsche and Best Buy which represent a new category of transformation partnerships," said Krithivasan. During the quarter, TCS announced the acquisition of Porsche's IT arm for $1.46 billion and US retailer Best Buy's GCC for an undisclosed sum. Revenue from these acquisitions will start flowing later this year.
Overall numbers were largely in line with analyst expectations, despite several quarters of muted growth driven by margin pressures and a slowdown in large deal wins.
An ET poll of analysts had pegged net profit growth at 9% from a year ago, while revenue was expected to gain about 13%. Sequentially, analysts had estimated a modest constant-currency revenue growth of 0.5-0.6%.
The September quarter also came with faster growth in AI revenue at $3.1 billion, which doubled from $1.5 billion in the second quarter last year, when the company first reported the category separately.
"We did quite well on AI revenues," said chief operating officer Aarthi Subramanian . "But if you look at traditional services, they did well too. Vendor consolidation and AI-powered software engineering, IT ops--how we innovate in execution is helping us differentiate and grow market share in traditional services as well."
For the September quarter, total contract value (TCV) was at $9.6 billion, marginally up from the preceding quarter's $9.5 billion. The growth came after its TCV saw a decline in the last three-month period.
Growth was led by the energy, resources and utilities sectors, which gained 5.7% YoY, followed by technology and services and the manufacturing sector, both of which grew over 4%. Banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI), its largest client segment accounting for 32.8% of revenue, gained 3.9%.
However, TCS' consumer segment continued its decline, falling 1%, as the sector remained sensitive to inflation and higher energy costs.
Among core markets, North America remained the leader with 48.3% revenue share, growing 1.5% on a yearly basis. The UK region accounted for 17.8% of revenue and recorded sharper 4.5% expansion, with the rest of Europe gaining 3.3%.
While the India market posted the steepest year-on-year growth at 6%, it was the only geography to record a fall on a sequential basis, down 10.3%. To be sure, the region accounts for just 5.5% of revenue.
"In India, we had a project deferral, which caused this revenue decrease. Otherwise, there is no structural issue. We are hoping to deliver these projects in subsequent quarters," Krithivasan said.
In FY26, TCS had posted its first annual revenue decline since listing-a 2.4% drop-showing the first signs of deflation in the IT sector.

docs.title: Lululemon puts Nike veteran in charge of product as CEO O'Neill looks to right ship
docs.text:
Lululemon Athletica on Wednesday named industry veteran and former Nike vice president Maggie Gauger its chief product officer as the struggling apparel maker overhauls its leadership under new CEO Heidi O'Neill .
 Investors are closely watching O'Neill's turnaround plan as the sportswear maker grapples with finding its footing against newer rivals and keep pace with changing customer preferences beyond its signature leggings.
Here are more details: 
* Gauger will join Lululemon on October 26, and was most recently CEO of Gap's performance apparel brand Athleta, following a long stint at Nike, alongside O'Neill
* Gauger takes charge of product at Lululemon at a time the company has struggled with product missteps that have triggered consumer backlash and recalls
 Live Events
* Lululemon also appointed Joseph Godsey as chief operating officer
* "This is an important first step in reinvigorating our enduring connection with guests and is designed to establish the foundation for sustainable, long-term growth," O'Neill said of the appointments
* Lululemon's shares have nearly halved in value so far this year, and are on track for a third straight year of declines
* The company's net income is expected to drop nearly 40% this year from fiscal 2024, according to data compiled by LSEG
* Lululemon also said chief brand officer Nikki Neuburger and chief supply chain officer Ted Dagnese would leave the company, effective November 6, and that it was searching for candidates to fill the roles
* It added that CFO Meghan Frank would oversee global brand and technology functions until those appointments are made

docs.title: GST reforms: Refunds, wider ITC mark third phase of reform as India targets global supply chains, says PwC
docs.text:
Nearly a decade since its roll out, the historic GST reform moved closer towards a pivotal point of maturity. Over the years, GST has largely evolved in two phases. While the first phase aimed at stabilisation of compliances, the second phase focused on rate rationalisation moving to a simplified three-tier rate structure in September 2025.
 The announcements made in the 57th council meeting launch the third phase of evolution that focuses on bolder policy reforms and ease of doing business at a time when India aspires to stage itself as a critical player in the global supply chain . Key themes emerging from the progressive announcements are unlocking corporate capital , liberalising GST credits, and easing out onerous compliance obligations .
A bold and aggressive decision made by the council is to ease severe working capital stress by broadening and expediting GST refunds . The September 2025 rate rationalisation exercise (GST 2.0) induced several sectors into an inverted rate structure, resulting in accumulation of GST credits. In such cases, refundscould only be claimed for ITC accumulated on raw material so far. The proposed framework will expand the scope to allow refunds for input services as well as capital goods. 
Another positive move is to allow GST credits on core business expenses like employees' insurance. This will help optimize the operational cost for businesses, especially the global capability centers.
A strong foundation has been laid for the next phase of transformative reforms, possibly GST 3.0 . which could target a phased inclusion of petroleum, power etc. and align with global best practices. The timing is also right and perhaps provides a much-neededstimulus to the economy and stock markets, as global uncertainties hover around.

docs.title: GST 2026: Simpler compliance, tech-led enforcement reflect growing trust between government and industry,
docs.text:
A key aspect underlining the GST Council meeting is the growing mutual trust between government and industry. Following the positive response to the September 2025 rate rationalisation exercise which drove steady growth in tax collections, the latest announcements build on that momentum by removing compliance friction and simplifying processes, expecting businesses to respond with stronger growth.
 The changes proposed highlight how technology can be harnessed to support business, proving the council's responsiveness amid global economic headwinds. The entire GST system is based on data provided by taxpayers, and it is befitting that the data collected is converted to information that is used to make compliance easier for all businesses.
The removal of arrest provisions from the GST legislation has been made possible only because it is now easier to identify tax evaders and fake ITC through the system. Similarly, the decision to constitute a committee of officers to examine how to protect ITC for genuine buyers and recover it from sellers who have not paid the tax, is possible due to the invoice matching trail. 
Both these measures are expected to remove a significant pain point. The simplification of registration provisions, the proposed system of annual return and quarterly payments for certain categories of business and the ease of correcting returns will bring more businesses onto the GST platform as they no longer fear a compliance-heavy business tax.
The changes reflect the growing trust between tax administration and business as both realise that growth in tax collections is dependent on growth in business which in turn is dependent on simpler tax processes and policies that recognise business practices and appreciate working capital challenges.

 Ever since she first appeared in Chand Ke Paar Chalo, Yami Gautam left viewers in enchanted with her beauty, dazzling smile and radiant skin. From her television days to silver-screen, the actress continues to opt for minimal-makeup that focuses on her natural features. However, her glowing skin has not come without its challenges. In an old post, the actress had admitted about living with Keratosis Pilaris, a skin condition she said has "no cure". So, how does she manage her skincare, despite her skin condition?
 Just like her makeup, Yami believes in simplicity even when it comes to skincare. It includes a humble kitchen staple she calls “magic.”
 Yami Gautam swears by this traditional skincare ingredient
For Gautam, skincare does not necessarily have to involve an elaborate routine or expensive products. The actress has previously spoken about her fondness for haldi, describing it as an old-school ingredient with a deeper traditional significance. When asked about a remedy she swears by, Gautam said, “Sacchi bataun? Haldi.” 
Explaining why turmeric continues to hold a special place in her routine, the actress said the ingredient is traditionally considered pure and auspicious. She also described haldi as “shubh” and said, “I want to get this tradition back,” as reported by Indian Express.
 Yami Gautam reveals her haldi and multani mitti experience
Gautam has also shared how she experimented with the traditional ingredient while shooting Haq. Speaking with MirchiPunjab, the actress revealed that her skin is “really sensitive.” During the film’s haldi ceremony, she decided to take the opportunity to try the ingredient herself. “Main haldi lagati hun,” she recalled saying, explaining that she wanted to see what would happen.
 You Might Also Like: 
 Yami Gautam's skin condition has 'no cure'. How the actress found the courage to accept her 'flaws'
The actress said she mixed a little multani mitti with haldi and even had before-and-after images that she planned to reveal later. According to Gautam, the combination “really worked like magic.” “For me, haldi is magic,” she said, adding that she is a fan of the ingredient and “swear[s] by it.”
 What does turmeric do for the skin?
Turmeric has also been studied for its potential skin-related properties. As per Healthline, turmeric contains antioxidants and anti-inflammatory components that may help provide the skin with glow and lustre. Healthline also notes that turmeric may help revive the skin and bring out its natural glow. One suggested at-home turmeric mask combines small amounts of Greek yogurt, honey and turmeric, which can be applied to the face for around 15 minutes before being washed off with water.
However, individual skin reactions can vary, particularly for people with sensitive skin.
 How to make Yami Gautam-inspired multani mitti and turmeric face pack
If you want to recreate the simple combination Gautam spoke about, the face pack requires just a few ingredients:
- 1 tbsp multani mitti
- ¼ tsp turmeric or haldi
- 1–2 tsp plain water or rose water
- A little plain yogurt, optional, if your skin tolerates it
Mix all the ingredients until you get a smooth paste. Apply a thin layer over the face, avoiding the corners of the eyes, and leave it on for around 5-10 minutes. Instead of letting the face pack to dry out completely, you can rinse it off right after 10 minutes. This will also prevent the skin from turning yellow. Make sure to follow it up with a moisturiser.
Those with sensitive skin should patch-test the mixture before applying it to the face. If burning, redness or itching occurs, wash it off and discontinue use.

docs.title: National Medical Commission bans doctors & hospitals from using AI-generated patient testimonials, fake cu
docs.text:
Under new ethical advertising guidelines issued by the National Medical Commission (NMC) on Tuesday and effective immediately, doctors and hospitals are strictly prohibited from using artificial intelligence to generate patient testimonials, fabricate clinical outcomes, or create promotional material. The regulation also bans healthcare providers from paying to manipulate search engine and app rankings.
 Crackdown on AI content and unverified claims 
The NMC has barred registered medical practitioners and hospitals from employing AI-generated content to advertise services, solicit patients, or disseminate unverifiable details concerning diagnoses, treatments, or patient results. Under the regulation, AI cannot be used to craft synthetic patient voices, testimonials, clinical outcomes, or fake endorsements, nor can it be used to misrepresent the quality or nature of medical services. 
Furthermore, medical professionals are barred from paying to manipulate search rankings or making unverified superlative claims such as "best", "number one", "most trusted", "guaranteed cures" or "100% success".
 Also read: Govt set to cap trade margins on more cancer drugs before SC hearing 
 Live Events
 Crackdown on paid patient solicitation and commercial schemes 
To protect patient interests, doctors are prohibited from entering financial arrangements with influencers, advertising agencies, or online platforms where payment is tied to procuring patients.
Additionally, hospitals and medical professionals cannot offer limited-period discounts, gift packages, coupons, or referral benefits that could incentivize unnecessary medical consultations. The guidelines also restrict using patient photographs without valid consent and safeguards, banning before-and-after imagery, patient testimonials, and treatment-success claims that risk creating unrealistic expectations or misleading the public.
However, the NMC clarified that doctors and hospitals remain permitted to use social media for non-promotional, objective, and factual health education.
 Also read: Drug panel rejects child images on cough syrup labels, proposes age warning for use below 4 years 
 Escalating penalties for non-compliance 
To ensure compliance, the NMC has outlined a progressive penalty framework for violations:
 First Violation: Formal warning and mandatory ethics training.
 Second Violation: Censure and monetary penalty.
 Third Violation: Suspension of license for three to six months.
 Serious Violations: Suspension of license for six to 12 months.
 Repeated Violations: Removal from the medical register for one to three years.

docs.title: Meet Brian Chesky, man who quit his stable job, struggled to pay rent, built Airbnb, faced investor reject
docs.text:
Brian Chesky had a good job, secure career, and a future that many people would have been happy with. But the industrial designer didn't feel satisfied with the path in front of him. He eventually left his job, moved to San Francisco with little money and took a chance on an unusual idea that started with a struggle to pay rent. That idea, which began with three mattresses in an apartment, eventually became Airbnb 
 The company transformed the way millions of people travel and turned Chesky into one of the world's best-know entrepreneurs. Today, he remains closely associated with the company he helped build from the ground up.
 Why did he leave his job?
Before becoming an entrepreneur , he worked as an industrial designer in Los Angeles after graduating from the Rhode Island School of Design (RISD). His education had encouraged him to believe that designers could create things that can change the world. 
However, his job left him questioning whether he wanted to spend his life following the same routine. In an interview with Startups .com, he recalled what he described as a "weird feeling of morality" while thinking about his daily life.
He said that he had reached a point where he thought, "This is my life." The office routine and commute made him wonder if there was something more he wanted to do.
 Live Events
Chesky then resigned from his job. He packed a foam bed into his Honda Civic and drove to San Francisco, where he planned a stay with his college friend Joe Gebbia.
 How did Airbnb's idea come up?
He arrived in San Francisco with very little money. He reportedly had around $1,000 in his bank account, while his share of the rent was higher than that amount.
Then an opportunity appeared in an unlikely form. A major design conference was scheduled to take place in San Francisco, bringing thousands of visitors to the city. Hotels were almost booked. Gebbia came up with an idea. The two friends could put mattresses in their apartment and rent the available space to conference visitors. They could also offer breakfast.
That small experiment became the starting point for Airbnb.
But, the start was difficult, as they struggled to convince investors. The founders accumulated thousands of dollars in credit card debt while facing repeated rejections.
In an unusual attempt to raise money, they created and sold specially designed cereal boxes linked to the 2008 US presidential election. The idea generated enough money to help them continue working in the setup.
They later took professional photographs of homes themselves. The simple change helped improve the listing and contributed to an increase in the bookings.
 What is his net worth?
According to Forbes, Brian Chesky's net worth is $11.3 billion.
What started as three mattresses in a San Francisco apartment became a global travel platform, as it connected hosts and guests around the world.

docs.title: Tea Research Association launches TocklAI, the world's first AI model for tea
docs.text:
Guwahati: The Tea Research Association (TRA) launched TocklAI , the world's first artificial intelligence model project built for the tea industry, at its 62nd Annual General Meeting at the Tollygunge Club, Kolkata.
 Pabitra Margherita, Union Minister of State for External Affairs and Textiles, Government of India attended the event. The meeting was held in the presence of C. Murugan, Deputy Chairman & CEO, Tea Board of India, and K. J. Patel, Managing Director, IFFCO. IFFCO also launched its nano fertilisers for tea at the meeting.
TocklAI draws on the research of TRA's Tocklai Tea Research Institute in Jorhat, Assam — the world's oldest and largest tea research station, now 115 years old. It is a small language model that uses retrieval-augmented generation: it answers from TRA's own verified research archive rather than general internet content, so its advice stays grounded in tested tea science and Indian growing conditions. 
Planters, managers and small growers can ask it practical questions on pest and disease control, soil health and nutrition, choice of clones, replanting, climate adaptation, processing and food-safety compliance.
TocklAI was conceived by Joydeep Phukan, Secretary of TRA, who leads the project, bringing together Tocklai's scientists, the Tea Board of India and Dr Vishal Misra of Columbia University.
 Live Events
 TRA's Council of Management approved the project on 24 July 2026."TRA Tocklai holds a century of data that no one else in the world has," said Suneel Singh Sikand, Chairman, Tea Research Association. "With TocklAI, that knowledge becomes a tool every planter and small grower can use. It is the first of its kind in the global tea industry, and we are proud that it comes from India."
"Small tea growers now produce more than half of India's tea, yet they have the least access to research," said Phukan. "TocklAI is designed to close that gap, and it will keep growing as our scientists add new findings. We have already digitised more than 2,000 scientific publications, and the work will be completed in 18 months."
Margherita said Assam is proud to be home to Tocklai, the world's oldest and largest tea research establishment, whose work has helped Northeast India nearly triple its tea output since 1951. Welcoming TocklAI, he said: "What could be more appropriate for an institution with 115 years of research behind it than to embrace one of the defining technologies of our time." He pointed to CHAAYANKAN, Tea Board India's new AI-based geospatial project with ISRO's National Remote Sensing Centre and NIT Rourkela to monitor plantations, forecast pests and diseases and estimate yields, as part of the same spirit of innovation. This, he said, reflects Prime Minister Narendra Modi's emphasis that India's future competitiveness depends on generating knowledge, adopting new technologies and turning research into outcomes. He noted the Government of Assam's support, including Rs 10 crore for Tocklai and Rs 17 crore for the Small Tea Growers' Cell.
He urged the industry to develop youth-friendly tea products and take Indian tea to higher-value global markets, with stronger traceability and compliance. "Tocklai has given 115 years to Indian tea. Our responsibility now is to ensure that the next century is equally remarkable," he said.
Sikand said exports rose to about 270 million kg worth over Rs 8,300 crore in 2025-26, but fell about 16 per cent in January–July 2026, hit by the West Asia conflict and shipping disruption.
He called compliance the defining issue for Indian tea. FSSAI MRLs for Acetamiprid and Imidacloprid, both approved for use in tea, are still pending, and the EU's new neonicotinoid rules have begun to affect shipments to Europe. TRA and the UK Tea & Infusions Association formed a Joint Working Group on 30 April 2026, joined by tea associations from Europe, the USA and Canada, to share regulatory intelligence.
Looking ahead, he warned that beyond 2037 India's production may not meet domestic consumption, citing a TRA study based on Tea Board data. He called for a national push on uprooting and replanting, backed by regenerative soil practices.
TRA released a climate-resilient clone, TV 36, which showed the least effect of climatic variation during breeding while retaining good yield potential.IFFCO launched Nano Urea Plus and Nano DAP for the tea industry. Four years of joint trials by TRA and IFFCO showed yield gains of 8–14 per cent, and both products will now enter TRA's Package of Practices.
A TRA study funded by the Tea Board through NTRF identified 397 flavour compounds that separate Darjeeling tea from seven other origins, including Nepal, giving a scientific basis for GI protection.
The FAO has entrusted TRA with a global framework on climate change and tea, towards a net-zero tea sector. TRA has proposed science centres in Assam and West Bengal to help small growers uproot and replant.

Synopsis
 The Delhi High Court recently upheld an eviction ruling that affects a daughter-in-law, amidst a nuanced legal struggle that weighs the interests of elderly individuals against those of women. This decision highlights key aspects of the Senior Citizens Act, sparking discussions on family rights, issues surrounding non-maintenance, and instances of mistreatment within housing conflicts.
 Listen to this article in summarized format
 Listen 
 In a judgment delivered on September 30, 2026, the Delhi High Court upheld an eviction order against a daughter-in-law and also upheld the validity of the Delhi rules that allow authorities to order eviction of children or legal heirs in cases involving non-maintenance or ill-treatment.
The case is significant because the court had to balance two competing protections: the senior citizen’s right to protection of life and property under the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act , 2007, and the daughter-in-law’s right to reside in a shared household under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act , 2005.
 What happened in the case? 
The petitioner was the daughter-in-law of the senior citizen. She had married the senior citizen’s son in 1996 and the couple had two children. Their marital relationship subsequently deteriorated. 
In August 2018, the daughter-in-law filed proceedings under the Domestic Violence Act against her husband and mother-in-law. She also sought a residence order under Section 19, claiming a right to reside in the property in Gautam Nagar, New Delhi, which she described as her shared household.
Around the same period, the senior citizen approached the authorities seeking eviction of her daughter-in-law under Rule 22(3)(1) of the Delhi Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Rules , 2009.
The Sub-Divisional Magistrate conducted an inquiry and reported that harassment by the daughter-in-law could not be established. The District Magistrate subsequently rejected the eviction application in February 2021.
The senior citizen appealed. The Divisional Commissioner took a different view and, in July 2022, directed the daughter-in-law to vacate the property and hand over peaceful possession to the senior citizen.
The daughter-in-law then approached the Delhi High Court.
 What did the daughter-in-law argue? 
She challenged both the eviction order and the validity of Rule 22(3)(1)(i) and (iv) of the Delhi Rules.
Her argument was that the Senior Citizens Act does not expressly provide for eviction and, therefore, the Delhi government could not create such a power through its rules.
She also argued that the eviction mechanism could not override her statutory right to reside in a shared household under Section 17 of the Domestic Violence Act.
“A daughter-in-law’s right to reside in a “shared household” under Sections 17 and 19 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, is a statutory right of residence and not an ownership or proprietary right. It does not automatically override the rights of a senior citizen who owns the property and seeks to live there peacefully,” explains Priya Gada, Advocate, D. M. Harish & Co. LLP.
However, the Senior Citizens Act does not automatically override the daughter-in-law’s rights under Section 17 of the Domestic Violence Act. The competing rights must be considered based on the facts of each case, she adds.
 What did the Delhi HC rule? 
The court rejected the challenge and examined Sections 21 and 22 of the Senior Citizens Act, which deal with measures for implementing the Act and protecting the life and property of senior citizens.
It held that the Delhi government's eviction rules were connected to this statutory objective and were within its rule-making powers.
Under Rule 22(3)(1), a senior citizen or parent can approach the Deputy Commissioner/District Magistrate seeking eviction of a son, daughter or legal heir from property on grounds including non-maintenance and ill-treatment.
The process requires verification of title and facts by the SDM (Sub-Divisional Magistrate). The occupant must also be given an opportunity to show cause before an eviction order is passed.
The court also held that the rule could extend to the family of a son or daughter, including a daughter-in-law, rather than interpreting the provision narrowly.
 Why did the court uphold eviction in this case? 
The court noted that the daughter-in-law was a postgraduate teacher with substantial income and had a separate house in Bahadurgarh. The senior citizen, on the other hand, wanted to live peacefully in her property and had complained that the continuing matrimonial dispute was affecting her life.
The court therefore found that the circumstances justified protecting the senior citizen's peaceful occupation.
The judgment does not mean that ownership automatically overrides a daughter-in-law's residence rights. Instead, the court considered factors such as alternative accommodation, financial circumstances and the senior citizen's need for peaceful living.
“In the above case the High Court emphasised that an elderly parent is entitled to lead a normal life and should not be compelled to spend the evening of her life being dragged into continuing matrimonial conflict between her son and daughter-in-law. The test therefore goes beyond physical violence and sustained harassment and destruction of peace within one's own home can also become relevant,” says Advocate Mayank Arora, Partner, The Chambers of Bharat Chugh.
 What does this mean for senior citizens? 
The judgment strengthens the ability of senior citizens in Delhi to seek protection when continued occupation of their property is accompanied by non-maintenance or ill-treatment.
However, it is not a blanket right to evict family members simply because the senior citizen owns the property. Authorities must examine the facts, allow the occupant to respond and consider competing legal rights.

docs.title: Uniqlo owner's Western bet pays off as profit surges 32%
docs.text:
Tokyo: Japan's Fast Retailing , owner of the global clothing brand Uniqlo, reported a forecast-beating 32% rise in annual profit on Thursday, driven by strong sales in North America and Europe, which together overtook China as its largest market for the first time. The shift marks a milestone for the retailer, which has relied on China as its largest overseas market for years, supported by nearly 900 Uniqlo stores.
 Its push into newer markets in recent years has helped cushion the impact of weakening sales in China, where a prolonged slowdown in consumer spending and intensifying competition from domestic brands have pressured foreign companies across sectors ranging from autos to luxury goods and retail.
Company founder and president Tadashi Yanai on Thursday reiterated a goal to reach annual sales of 10 trillion ($63.2 billion), up from under 4 trillion in the just-completed year, by adding about 500 billion each year. 
"When you say 500 billion, in our clothing retail sector, that's a massive company," Yanai said. "It's roughly the equivalent of one such company being created every year," he said.
"If you look around the world, there are regions everywhere with that sort of potential."
 Live Events
Yanai, Japan's richest man, has long said he wants to make Fast Retailing the world's top clothing retailer, putting the company in competition with Zara owner Inditex and Sweden's H&M.
Combined revenue from North America and Europe reached 877.6 billion, surpassing 724 billion it earned from greater China.

Nifty ended Friday with sharp cuts amid selling pressure across the board, with consumer, IT and energy stocks dragging the markets the most. India VIX also moved back above its 200-DMA, indicating rising fear among the market participants. 
 Commenting on the technical charts, Rupak De, Senior Technical Analyst at LKP Securities, said that the setup has turned relatively cautious, with the index slipping below its 20-DMA for the first time in the past few sessions. Additionally, it has breached the 38.2% Fibonacci retracement of the prior up move from 24,571 to 26,341, he added. "With the index closing below the key support level of 25,500, the near-term bias appears weak, and there is potential for a decline toward the 25,000 mark in the short term. On the upside, immediate resistance is seen around 25,800," De said.
Here are 2 stock recommendations for Friday:
 Buy Kirloskar Oil Engines at Rs 1,375-1,385 | Upside: 5% | Target: Rs 1,500 | Stop Loss: Rs 1,320
 Kirloskar Oil Engines is currently taking a breakout of the rounding bottom formation on the daily time frame. The RSI is trending upward, reflecting positive momentum, and the stock finds support at the 21-day EMA, with all key EMAs rising. The stock is trading above important moving averages, indicating a bullish trend. 1,320 could work as an immediate support, and a hurdle can be seen at 1,500.
 (Drumil Vithlani, Technical Research Analyst, Bonanza Portfolio) 
 Buy Bajaj Finance at Rs 1,024-1,026 | Upside: 4% | Stop Loss: Rs 990 | Target: Rs 1,070
 Bajaj Finance is currently taking a breakout of the downward-moving channel on the daily time frame. The lower trend line has provided support, accompanied by the formation of a bullish candlestick pattern, indicating a potential short-term upward movement in the stock. Momentum Indicator RSI is trading near the overbought region, which confirms the bullishness in the script.

As preparations for the Union Budget 2026–27 gather pace, the groundwork underway signals a clear policy intent to accelerate domestic demand, revive private investment and generate employment, according to a budget note by Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL). The brokerage has identified five stocks across auto, agriculture, defence, financials and infrastructure themes, which it believes could deliver strong gains for investors.
 "The Budget is expected to focus on income-tax, GST, and customs simplification to enhance ease of doing business and support fiscal consolidation, alongside targeted support for agriculture, MSMEs, manufacturing, infrastructure, higher defence capex, EVs, and renewables through credit and incentives," the note authored by Research Analysts Sneha Poddar and Rekha Jaat said.
A strong capital expenditure thrust across highways, logistics, defence, rail freight corridors and connectivity is anticipated, complemented by emphasis on skilling, rural prosperity, women empowerment, AI adoption, climate action and digital finance to anchor India’s next phase of economic expansion, the note added.
The finance ministry started work on the Union Budget for 2026-27 from October 9 as per a circular issued by the Department of Economic Affairs (DEA).
The preparations come against the backdrop of an additional 50% US tariff on most Indian goods and other external headwinds. These have raised risks to India's growth and jobs outlook, prompting calls for stronger support to the export sector.
 Live Events
 5 stocks to buy: 
The stocks recommended by MOFSL are TVS Motor Company, UPL , Bharat Dynamics (BDL), M&M Financial Services and Dalmia Bharat , and each of these stocks has been assigned a 20% weight.
 1) TVS Motors: TVS Motors continues to outperform peers and is well-positioned to benefit from the budget’s push to boost domestic consumption and rural demand through higher allocations, income support, and infrastructure spending.
MOFSL said that improving rural sentiment, strong entry-level recovery and sustained two-wheeler demand will be key triggers. Moreover, the company's market share gains, easing discounts, and margin expansion will provide strong earnings visibility. The Apache and Ntorq maker remains its top pick in OEMs.
 2) UPL: The diversified agrochemical leader is well positioned to benefit from the union budget push riding on rural prosperity via higher agri credit, MSME support, and value-chain strengthening, lifting farmer incomes and crop-protection demand.
The company's strong points are stronger volumes, export tailwinds, improved working-capital discipline and post-bond-repayment balance-sheet strength, the brokerage note said. The company's rising focus on speciality chemicals supports solid 2HFY26 growth.
 3) Bharat Dynamics: Bharat Dynamics (BDL), a defence play, has a robust Rs 50,000 crore order pipeline over five years, with Rs 20,000 crore targeted in 2-3 years. This aligns with the expected defence capex surge and infra push.
The recent Rs 2.5 lakh crore DAC approvals for missiles, undersea warfare, and naval arms leverage BDL's tactical/strategic expertise, propelling FY31 turnover to Rs 100bn via indigenisation and lower provisions, the note said.
 4) M&M Financial Services: M&M Financial is poised for Union Budget 2026-27 benefits via rural prosperity, MSME credit, and employment focus, driving PV/tractor loan growth amid surging volumes from festive demand, GST cuts, and restocking.
The company targets Rs 3 lakh crore in assets under management (AUM) by 2030, which is at an 18-20% CAGR, bolstered by AI underwriting, lower credit costs, controlled opex, and margin stability for strong earnings visibility in retail portfolios.
 5) Dalmia Bharat: The cement company benefits from the budget’s infra capex surge, PMAY rural housing, and urban projects, driving cement volume growth.
Dalmia Bharat is a low-cost cement producer with high blending ratios, green power and low freight. The company is targeting 62 mtpa capacity by FY28, and its cost optimisation endeavours will likely lift EBITDA margins amid sector consolidation.

Reliance Power 's board of directors on Monday approved the issuance of up to 46.20 crore equity shares/warrants worth Rs 1,525 crore via preferential allotment mode.
 The board has set the issue price at Rs 33 per share.
The issue price of equity shares/warrants is at a discount of 13% over Monday's closing price of Rs 38.15 on the NSE. The announcement was made after market hours and Reliance Power shares on Monday ended with gains of Rs 1.81 or 4.98% over the previous closing price.
 Reliance Infrastructure Limited, the promoter of the company, will enhance its equity stake by over Rs 600 crore, a company filing said. The other investors in the preferential issue are Authum Investment and Infrastructure Limited and Sanatan Financial Advisory Services Private Limited.
The proceeds from the preferential issue will be utilised to expand business operations directly and/or through investment in subsidiaries and joint ventures, debt reduction and for general corporate purposes, the filing said.

The markets worldwide are waiting with bated breath on what will be a historic policy announcement from the US Federal Reserve , where the central bank is expected to usher in a rate cut cycle.
 The announcement will be made at 11:30 pm IST (Indian Standard Time) on Wednesday.
If analysts are to be believed, the US Fed is all but certain to cut interest rates for the first time in more than four years.
However, there is no consensus on the quantum of reduction. Some are predicting a smaller cut of a quarter of a percentage point, while others believe a bigger half-point reduction is in the works.
Senior officials at the US central bank, including Powell, have indicated that a rate cut is coming, as inflation eases toward the bank's long-term target of 2%, and the labour market continues to cool in the post-Covid economy.
 Live Events
If the Fed starts the rate cut cycle, the Reserve Bank of India is also expected to follow suit.
A smaller cut would be a more predictable move, while a bigger cut would do more to boost demand — while also running the risk of reigniting inflation.
 WATCH LIVE TODAY: Press conference with #FOMC Chair Powell at 2:30 p.m. ET: https://t.co/1uJrua5qsH https://t.co/FJa6TbkDMt pic.twitter.com/87g5NJITsz 
— Federal Reserve (@federalreserve) September 18, 2024 
By the end 2024, markets are expecting a total reduction of at least 100 basis points in the first rate cut cycle in over 4 years since 2020.
But whether the Fed goes for 25 or 50 bps, the biggest trigger for stock prices to move up or down would be Powell's motivation behind the cut.
Asset classes from stocks, currencies and fixed income could all log swings in the immediate aftermath of the Fed decision.
While easing US interest rates are directionally positive for equities in general, “we should keep in mind interest rates are just one variable in a complex adaptive system that determines the direction of Indian equity markets”, said Anoop Vijaykumar, Investments and Head of Research at Capitalmind.

Nomura maintains Mahindra & Mahindra and Ather as its top picks in passenger vehicles and two-wheelers, respectively, as it expects Ather, TVS Motor and Eicher Motors to potentially beat 2QFY27 estimates. TMPV and Ashok Leyland could miss estimates, while among auto ancillaries, Sona Comstar, Bharat Forge, Motherson and Motherson Sumi Wiring India could surprise positively.
Nomura also maintains its 'Buy' ratings on Hyundai Motor India and TVS Motor , while preferring Sona Comstar and Uno Minda among auto suppliers.
Domestic volume growth remained robust in 2QFY27, with MHCVs growing 34% year-on-year, followed by passenger vehicles at 30%, LCVs at 23% and two-wheelers at 14%. Tractor volumes declined 5% year-on-year.
The brokerage said the "more significant trend" was the continued acceleration in EV adoption, with EV penetration above 7% for passenger vehicles and above 11% for two-wheelers. It expects this trend to continue through 2HFY27F, with EV penetration rising across both segments.
"Companies with relatively high EV exposure, competitive products and established EV technology should be better placed to grow well ahead of the industry," Nomura said, while incumbents with predominantly ICE-led portfolios could face increasing market share pressure.
Nomura expects elevated commodity and metal prices to keep margins under pressure in 2QFY27F, although the impact should vary across segments.
"Commodity cost inflation remains the key near-term headwind," it said, adding that the full impact of elevated commodity prices is yet to flow through for OEMs.
CV and tractor margins are likely to see a higher sequential impact, while two-wheelers are expected to largely pass on the cost pressures. Passenger vehicle OEMs may continue to face margin pressure due to higher competitive intensity.
Nomura expects the margin trajectory to improve as price hikes catch up with the commodity cycle.
For its covered OEMs, excluding unlisted Jaguar Land Rover, Nomura expects cumulative revenue growth of 30% year-on-year and EBITDA growth of 11%, with EBITDA margins rising 30 basis points sequentially to 11.5%.
It expects Ather to report a slight sequential margin improvement despite steep cost pressure, while M&M's Auto EBIT, including BEV and ICE, is expected to grow 32% year-on-year.
For covered auto ancillaries, revenue is expected to rise 26% year-on-year and 7% sequentially, supported by healthy OEM production and price hikes to offset higher commodity costs. EBITDA growth is expected at 19% year-on-year, with the tyre sector a key drag.
"Rising commodity and labour costs and partial pass-through should keep margins lower than in the past," Nomura said. It also expects higher freight costs to weigh on margins for exporters.
Compared with Bloomberg consensus estimates, Nomura expects Ather, TVS Motor and Eicher Motors to beat 2QFY27 estimates, while TMPV and Ashok Leyland could miss.
Among auto ancillaries, Sona Comstar, Bharat Forge, Motherson and Motherson Sumi Wiring India are likely to "surprise positively", while Balkrishna Industries could disappoint.

 EverestIMS Technologies shares make strong debut at 48% premium on BSE SME
 Shares of EverestIMS Technologies made a strong debut on the BSE SME platform on October 8, listing at Rs 126 per share. 
 October 08, 2026 / 11:22 IST 
 Story continues below Advertisement
 Remove Ad 
 EverestIMS Technologies Share Price 
 EverestIMS shares debuted at Rs 126, up 48.23% from IPO.
 The IPO was subscribed 273.67 times on the final day.
 The company raised Rs 48.45 crore through the IPO.
 Did our AI summary help? 
 Market Mastery
Shares of EverestIMS Technologies made a strong debut on the BSE SME platform on October 8, listing at Rs 126 per share.
The stock opened at a premium of Rs 41, or 48.23 percent, over its initial public offering (IPO) price of Rs 85 per share.
 However, the listing gain was lower than the grey market premium (GMP) indicated ahead of the debut. The shares were commanding a GMP of around 74 percent on October 7, according to InvestorGain.
 Read Also: Vishal Nirmiti shares list at 2% discount to IPO price on BSE, NSE — should you buy, sell or hold? 
The GMP is an unofficial indicator of investor sentiment in the unlisted market and is not regulated by stock exchanges. It can change before listing, and the actual listing price may differ from the price implied by the GMP.
 The strong listing followed an overwhelming response to the company's IPO, which was subscribed 273.67 times on the final day of bidding on October 5.
The company raised Rs 48.45 crore through the IPO, which comprised 57 lakh shares offered in a price band of Rs 80-85 per share.
The issue included a fresh issue of 45.93 lakh shares and an offer-for-sale (OFS) of 11.07 lakh shares by promoters and employees.
 Investors placed bids for 111.87 crore equity shares against the 40.88 lakh shares available for subscription, through 2.04 lakh applications.
Demand was particularly strong in the non-institutional investors (NIIs) category, which was subscribed 406.34 times. The retail portion was subscribed 268.29 times, while the qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) category was subscribed 148.63 times.
At the upper end of the price band, the IPO attracted bids worth around Rs 9,510 crore, significantly exceeding the amount the company sought to raise.
At the IPO price of Rs 85 per share, EverestIMS Technologies was valued at around Rs 184 crore.
The company plans to use a portion of the net proceeds from the fresh issue to purchase IT
hardware for setting up an artificial intelligence innovation and experience laboratory during the current financial year.
Around Rs 5.65 crore has been earmarked for this purpose, while Rs 24 crore will be used to meet the company's working capital requirements.
The remaining funds will be utilised for general corporate purposes.
EverestIMS Technologies provides software-as-a-service (SaaS) and on-premises software products and services focused on digital transformation, IT operations and service management.
The company also offers AI-enabled product solutions and plans to strengthen its artificial intelligence capabilities through the proposed innovation and experience laboratory.

 Stock market recap: Indian equities suffered a broad-based selloff on Thursday, 8 October, as surging crude prices, a weaker rupee and the RBI’s hawkish turn kept investors on edge. The Nifty 50 fell 371.25 points, or 1.64%, to 22,231.80, after hitting a fresh 52-week low of 22,179.90 during the session. The Sensex dropped 1,045.46 points, or 1.44%, to 71,593.24.
 Brent crude rose above $104 a barrel on concerns over supply from West Asia, while the rupee weakened past 97 to the dollar and rising US bond yields added to the pressure. Foreign investors sold ₹ 6,121 crore of shares on Wednesday.
 Metals, capital goods , healthcare, and oil and gas stocks bore the brunt of the selloff. IT was the only sector to remain resilient, with TCS gaining about 2.6% ahead of its quarterly results. Adani Enterprises and JSW Steel were among the biggest Nifty losers, while ITC fell more than 4% after a large block deal. Oil-sensitive stocks including HPCL, BPCL and IndiGo also declined sharply.
 Market breadth was deeply negative, with 660 stocks advancing, 2,950 declining and 112 unchanged. TCS’s results, due tonight, will provide the first major test of investor sentiment as the earnings season gets underway.
 Two stock recommendations by MarketSmith India: 
 Buy: Netweb Technologies India Ltd (current price: ₹ 4,715) 
 Why it’s recommended: AI infrastructure expansion, strong order book, hpc, and private cloud opportunities. 
 Key metrics: P/E: 106.86, 52-week high: ₹ 5,813, volume: ₹ 23.38 lakhs

 Risk factors: Margin pressure, execution and working capital risks, order concentration and valuation risk 
 Buy: ₹ 4,668–4,739

 Key metrics: P/E: 12.74, 52-week high: ₹ 1,211.50, volume: ₹ 221.35 crore 
 Technical analysis: Reclaimed 50 DMA 
 Risk factors: Interest-rate and margin pressure, rising borrowing costs, higher-risk affordable-loan expansion, corporate-lending re-entry risk 
 Buy at: ₹ 1,139-1,156 
 Target price: ₹ 1,290 in two to three months 
 Stop loss: ₹ 1,090 
 How Nifty 50 performed 
 Indian equity markets suffered a sharp sell-off on Thursday, with the Nifty 50 falling 371.25 points, or 1.64%, to 22,231.80. The index opened at 22,599.05 and remained under sustained selling pressure, touching an intraday low of 22,179.90—a fresh 52-week low.
 Selling was broad-based, with Nifty Metal falling 3.55%, Realty 3.16%, Media 2.79%, Oil & Gas 2.52% and Auto 2.49%. FMCG and Pharma declined 2.02% and 2.32%, respectively, while IT was relatively resilient, slipping just 0.08%. Market breadth was deeply negative, with 660 stocks advancing, 2,950 declining and 112 unchanged, an advance-decline ratio of roughly 1:4.5.
 The sell-off reflected growing concerns over tighter RBI monetary policy, elevated crude oil prices, persistent foreign institutional selling, and the conflict in West Asia.
 Technical outlook 
 The Nifty remains firmly in a bearish trend, with the index forming a lower-high, lower-low structure and trading below its key short-, medium- and long-term moving averages. The break below its previous consolidation zone, following an earlier breach of the rising trendline, further reinforces the negative setup.
 The RSI at 27.55 has entered oversold territory, signalling intense selling momentum but also leaving room for a near-term technical rebound. Oversold conditions, however, do not by themselves indicate a trend reversal. The MACD remains firmly negative, with the MACD line at -368.57 below the signal line at -324.60 and a negative histogram of -43.97, confirming continued bearish momentum.
 The index also breached its previous swing low of 22,217, falling to 22,180. The 22,200–22,000 zone remains the key near-term support; a decisive break below it could extend the decline towards 21,700–21,600. On the upside, 22,600–22,800 is likely to act as resistance, with any recovery towards this zone potentially attracting fresh selling.

 The index formed a bearish candle with a lower shadow, indicating some buying near the day’s low but continued seller dominance. It remains below all key moving averages, keeping the technical structure weak, while elevated volume of 224.84 million reinforced the decline. A sequence of lower highs also points to a firmly downward near-term trend. Unless Nifty Bank reclaims the 55,000–55,625 zone, rallies are likely to attract selling.
 The RSI stood at 36.45, below its average line of 37.84 and approaching oversold territory, signalling weak momentum without yet indicating an extreme condition. The MACD remained firmly below zero, with the MACD line at -629.31 below the signal line at -586.41. The negative histogram of -42.90 confirms that bearish momentum remains intact, although its relatively modest size suggests selling pressure is not accelerating sharply. No bullish divergence is visible. A sustained move in RSI above 40, alongside a bullish MACD crossover, would point to improving short-term momentum.

docs.title: This Adani Group share is among Jefferies India's top 3 picks despite the RBI's 25 bps Repo Rate hike
docs.text:
In the latest Jefferies India report dated 7 October 2026, it is highlighted that monetary tightening will negatively impact the profitability of power companies. However, after a detailed analysis of Indian power companies and their loan exposures based on fixed and floating interest rates, the global investment bank has retained its faith in three Indian power stocks: Adani Energy Solutions , JSW Energy , and NTPC . Highlighting the potential EPS impact on the Indian power companies due to the 25 bps Repo Rate hike, Jefferies India report said, “Power companies have some protection against hikes between regulated equity, fixed rate loans and lower rate hike pass through. NTPC, Power Grid and Adani Energy (AESL) should see 2-4% FY28E-30E EPS impact on 100 bps rate rise, while Adani Green could see 15%+.” The Jefferies India report has highlighted that NTPC and Power Grid have 36-57% loans on a fixed vs floating rate basis. Additionally, they have the advantage of more than 70% of their gross block base being on a regulated return, with interest cost pass-through. This materially limits the EPS impact. AESL's impact appears limited, as 65%+ of its loans are fixed-rate. Adani Green is highly leveraged at 6.5-6.6x net debt-to-equity, which makes the impact the highest in our coverage universe. However, management’s strategy of continuing to move toward long-tenor fixed-rate loans overseas and refinancing loans once assets are operational should help mitigate the perceived impact. Jefferies India believes that power demand is up 10% YoY YTD, with generation in Sept 2026up 13% YoY. Recent news reports (New Indian Express, 03 Oct 2026) indicate that El-Nino could continue in CY27, which points to the CY26 peak deficit repeating in CY27. Mint Money 
 Your money, shown at one place: What RBI’s new AA measures mean
 Ananya Grover 4 min read 8 Oct 2026, 02:01 PM IST 
 Summary
 The expanded consolidated account statement will include bank deposits, while account aggregator interoperability aims to make financial-data sharing simpler. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is moving to give consumers a fuller picture of their finances in one place, by bringing bank deposits into the monthly consolidated account statement (CAS) and allowing greater interoperability among account aggregators.
 The changes, announced in the October monetary policy review, are aimed at making it easier for consumers to see, track and share financial information across institutions. Both the measures are to be implemented by 31 December, the RBI said.
 The CAS, issued by depositories, regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India ( Sebi ), currently brings together investments such as mutual funds, equity shares, bonds and government securities linked to an investor’s Permanent Account Number (PAN), along with holdings, transactions and valuations. The expanded statement will also include savings, fixed and recurring deposits through the account aggregator (AA) framework.
 An AA is a regulated financial technology framework that allows customers to digitally share financial information between institutions with their explicit consent.
 A fuller financial picture 
 The move addresses a basic gap in the CAS: while it shows a person’s investments, it does not currently provide a consolidated view of bank deposits.
 Speaking at the post-policy press conference on Wednesday, RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said the monthly statement would allow consumers to see all their holdings at a glance. Adding deposits, he said, fills a missing piece in that picture.
 Malhotra also pointed to a more practical problem: bank deposits can be lost or go unclaimed when an account holder dies because family members may not know the accounts exist. A single statement showing deposits alongside other investments could give nominees and legal heirs a clearer record of the assets held by the deceased, making them easier to trace and claim.
 BG Mahesh, chief executive of Sahamati, said, “Adding bank deposit information to the Consolidated Account Statement will give customers a fuller picture of their finances in one place. Although this is already available via many regulated financial institutions. Through AA and with customer’s consent, CAS can go beyond reporting securities holdings and include bank deposit, insurance, NPS, GST details. This extends the role of depositories from reporting investments to helping customers see investments and deposits together.”
 Sahamati is RBI-recognized self-regulatory organization for India's account aggregator open finance ecosystem.
 The broader implication is that the CAS could evolve from a statement of securities holdings into a more comprehensive record of a person’s financial assets.
 Breaking the AA connectivity barrier 
 Separately, the central bank has allowed interoperability among account aggregators of non-banking financial companies ( NBFCs ), enabling financial information to be aggregated across account aggregators.
 Mahesh said there are currently 17 operational AAs. While Sebi-regulated financial information providers connect to all AAs, many providers in banking and insurance connect to only three or four, limiting customers’ choice of aggregator.
 “Interoperability removes that connectivity barrier, allowing customers to use their chosen AA and service providers to serve them without requiring another AA registration,” he said.
 Until now, for example, a customer whose bank was not connected to their preferred AA may have had to register with another aggregator to share that data. Interoperability should reduce that friction by allowing customers to use their preferred AA even when the relevant financial institution is connected through another aggregator.
 That could also reduce the number of registrations and consent dashboards customers have to manage. For lenders, advisers and other service providers, the change could widen access to financial information from institutions that were previously outside their AA network.
 Venkatesh Krishnamoorti, founder of SAAFE Account Aggregator, said a major obstacle to the AA ecosystem’s growth had been the lack of interoperability, which forced customers to create multiple accounts with different AAs to access and share their financial data.
 “This not only hindered effective consent management but also prevented customers from engaging with their preferred AA for all their needs,” he added.
 Varoon Naidu, co-founder of Capital Stack, said the changes should, over time, improve the availability and quality of credit, reduce turnaround times and potentially allow lenders to price risk more accurately.
 “The real impact, however, will depend on how seamlessly interoperability is implemented across account aggregators, lenders, and financial information providers,” he added.
 The RBI governor described the AA framework as an important tool because it gives individuals an overview of their financial assets in one place.
 "With consent from the individual, this information can be shared with other users too, such as insurers, brokers, asset managers and investment advisors, who can then offer more appropriate advice," he said.
 Most banks have already been onboarded on the framework, he added, while the remaining financial institutions will join over time.
 The two changes together could make the AA ecosystem more useful to consumers: the expanded CAS would give them a broader view of what they own, while interoperability would make it easier to access and share that information through their preferred aggregator.

Mint Money RBI rate hike: What it means for loans, deposits and markets Joydeep Sen 3 min read 8 Oct 2026, 09:26 AM IST Summary The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) opts for a precautionary rate hike to curb demand as inflation is set to inch up. Gift this article Check your portfolio This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you. Subscribe to enjoy similar stories. Subscribe now In the run-up to the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) monetary policy review, there was widespread expectation that the interest rate hike cycle would begin. Inflation is inching up and is likely to move up further. Globally, central banks are raising interest rates and bond yields are at multi-decade highs. The RBI did the expected. The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) hiked repo rate by 25 basis points (0.25%) to 5.50%. The repo rate is the rate at which the RBI lends money to banks. This rate is the pivot for interest rates across the system. By raising the repo rate, the RBI has signalled that bank deposit and lending rates should move up. Apart from the rate decision, the RBI also signals its stance on the future course of monetary policy . This stance was changed from neutral to ‘calibrated tightening’. It was mentioned that ‘policy action ahead can only be a rate hike or a pause, depending on the evolving conditions and the outlook’. This means the RBI could raise rates further depending on the inflation outlook. The RBI raised its inflation projection for 2026-27 to an average of 5.2% in the latest review, from 5% projected in its 5 August policy review. The encouraging part on growth was that the RBI raised its GDP growth projection for 2026-27 to an average of 7.1%, from 6.7% projected in August. This is a substantial rise. India's GDP grew at an unexpected 7.8% pace during the April-June quarter (Q1). Economists are now revising their growth projections upwards. What lies ahead To state the obvious, further rate hikes lie ahead. The question is the extent of those hikes. Given that the projected inflation for 2026-27 is 5.2%, and that for April-June 2027 is 5.6%, at least another rate hike of 25 basis points is due, probably in the next review on 4 December 2026. The rationale is that inflation is expected to average 6% in the October-December quarter, touching the upper end of the RBI’s 2-6% target range. Thereafter, RBI may either hit a pause or hike one last time after December, depending on how inflation pans out. Post December, inflation is expected to moderate, averaging 5.7% in January-March 2027 and 5.6% in April to June 2027. Impact on bank deposits, loans Loan rates, particularly those on floating rates, would rise. The interest rate reset happens faster in floating rate loans. Usually, bank deposit rates would also be expected to rise following an RBI rate hike. That would happen gradually, over a period of time. At this juncture, banking system liquidity is very high and banks are in no hurry to attract more deposits. This is because banks have seen large inflows into FCNR (B) deposits . They have swapped these dollar-denominated deposits with the RBI, receiving rupee liquidity in return. Going forward, it is expected that banking system liquidity would normalize from the current surplus state, and that is when we can expect better deals on bank deposits. Impact on markets Theoretically, higher interest rates are bad for both equity and bond markets. The logic is that higher interest rates raise the cost of money, leaving less money available to invest in stocks. However, currently, there are other overwhelming factors. Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have pulled out big time. Higher-yielding bonds abroad, particularly in the US, are an option for FPIs, apart from emerging market equity. However, there is buying support from domestic institutional investors (DIIs), particularly through mutual fund systematic investment plans (SIPs). SIP inflows are concentrated more in small- and mid-cap funds, while FPIs have been selling more large-cap stocks. On balance, higher interest rates are unlikely to have much incremental impact on the current market dynamics. Rate hikes are negative for bonds, as yields in the secondary market tend to rise when the RBI signals higher interest rates, hurting bond prices. However, the bond market was already prepared for this hike. The 10-year government bond yield, even before the latest repo rate hike, was at 7.2%. Yields have moved up after the hike, but only marginally. Joydeep Sen is a corporate trainer (financial markets) and author. docs.title: RBI rate hike: How higher rates will impact your EMIs, FDs and debt funds
docs.text:
Mint Money 
 RBI rate hike: How higher rates will impact your EMIs, FDs and debt funds
 Shipra Singh 8 min read 8 Oct 2026, 02:19 PM IST 
 Summary
 For borrowers, this would mean higher interest rates on home, vehicle and personal loans, while savers could benefit from better returns on fixed deposits. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) increased the repo rate by 25 basis points (1 basis point or bps is equal to 0.01%) to 5.50% on Wednesday, its first hike since February 2023. The hike was a result of accelerating inflation and geopolitical uncertainty that has pushed up crude oil prices. 
 More importantly, the Monetary Policy Committee shifted its stance from ‘neutral’ to ‘calibrated tightening.’ Indranil Pan, chief economist at Yes Bank, said ‘calibrated tightening’ indicates another hike or a pause. Economists peg the hike at anywhere from 25 bps to 100 bps cumulatively in the current fiscal year. 
 For borrowers, this would mean higher interest rates on home, vehicle and personal loans, while savers could benefit from better returns on fixed deposits (FDs) and bonds.
 Impact on borrowers 
 Floating-rate home loans linked to the repo rate will be directly affected, impacting both existing and new borrowers. Lenders have started increasing rates on new loans, particularly with the festive season approaching. As of Thursday, Punjab National Bank, Bank of Baroda, Bank of India and Indian Bank, among others, had increased their repo-linked benchmark lending rate (RBLR) by 25 bps. 
 “I expect the increase to be passed on immediately for new customers. State Bank of India will announce its quarterly rate changes by 15 October and other major banks are likely to follow,” said Mangesh Zope, founder of Peaceful-Loans. 
 For existing borrowers, the transmission can vary across lenders, depending on the reset terms. 
 “SBI’s loan agreement says rates linked to the EBLR (external benchmark linked rate) reset on the 15th of every month, while ICICI Bank resets rates once a quarter. NBFCs could pass on the increase faster as it’s a rate hike,” said Zope. 
 Once the higher interest rate takes effect, lenders typically extend loan tenures and keep EMIs unchanged. This doesn’t mean the EMI can’t be increased—borrowers have to ask the lender to revise the EMI .
 “A 25-bps hike’s impact will not be significant. At 7.5% over 25 years, the monthly EMI could rise by about ₹ 490 on a ₹ 30 lakh loan, ₹ 654 on ₹ 40 lakh and ₹ 817 on ₹ 50 lakh,” said Adhil Shetty, CEO of BankBazaar. 
 But with another hike or a pause likely, borrowers should keep an eye on the loan tenure, Shetty added. 
 “Many lenders extend the tenure to keep the EMI unchanged, which feels easier but costs more over time,” he said. 
 A longer tenure results in higher interest outgo. Take the example of a ₹ 50 lakh loan at 7.75% with a 20-year tenure. If the rate rises to 8% and the EMI is unchanged, the tenure will increase by eleven months, and the borrower would pay about ₹ 3 lakh in additional interest than if the EMI was increased and the original tenure was retained. Keeping the tenure unchanged will increase the monthly EMI by about ₹ 775. 
 Stretched repayment 
 When the rate rises but the EMI is unchanged, a larger portion of the EMI goes towards interest and less towards principal, which means the outstanding principal declines more slowly, stretching the repayment period and increasing the total interest paid over the loan tenure. 
 The impact is sharper if rate hikes are over 50 bps. In the example cited, if the loan rate rises from 7.75% to 8.5% and the EMI remains unchanged, the tenure would increase by almost three years and the borrower would pay about ₹ 10 lakh more in interest, compared to keeping the original 20-year tenure unchanged and increasing the EMI. 
 This impact will be pronounced for borrowers with a long repayment period ahead because interest continues to accrue on the outstanding principal for more years. For borrowers with less than 20%-30% of their total loan tenure left, the impact is less because most of the interest would already have been repaid. 
 As rates rise, Zope recommends increasing the EMI rather than extending the tenure if monthly cash flows permit. Shetty concurred and added small prepayments can be made every year to help limit the extra interest. 
 The rate hike could also affect new vehicle and personal loans, although the transmission is less direct than for repo-linked home loans. Higher policy rates push up lenders’ funding costs, which results in the repricing of new loans. 
 “New borrowers may see lenders reprice loans based on their funding costs and the borrower’s risk profile. Existing borrowers with floating rate personal and vehicle loans could see rates rise if lenders pass on the increase, while fixed rate borrowers may not see an immediate change,” said Shetty. 
 Impact on depositors 
 For savers, a rising interest-rate cycle can improve returns on new FDs. However, Shetty said deposit rates do not move in lockstep with the repo rate. 
 “Banks decide how much to raise FD rates based on their need for deposits, liquidity and competition for funds. This means a 25-bps repo rate hike need not translate into a similar increase in FD rates,” he said. 
 Currently, major private banks offer 6.3-7% on deposits of below ₹ 1 crore with tenures of one to two years, while some small finance banks offer rates of up to 8.1%. 
 “For depositors, this could keep FD rates firm and create some scope for upward repricing,” Shetty added. 
 Existing FDs will continue to earn the rate at which they were booked, so depositors will benefit from higher rates only when they make a fresh deposit or renew a maturing one. With further rate hikes likely, one option is to stagger deposits across maturities, allowing portions of the money to be reinvested if rates move high

News 
 Creators are changing fashion shopping. Myntra is going all in
 Varuni Khosla 4 min read 8 Oct 2026, 11:14 AM IST 
 Summary
 Myntra aims to outpace the growth of India's social-commerce market by enhancing product discovery through video content. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 Indian fashion shopping is increasingly shifting from search-led to discovery-led purchases, with consumers buying products they encounter through videos and creator content rather than products they were actively looking for.
 That shift is becoming a meaningful business for Myntra. Creator-led and social commerce now account for about 10% of its revenue, a business that did not exist in its current form about two years ago.
 The Flipkart -owned fashion platform, which started selling through creators in December 2024, expects this part of its business to grow faster than India’s social-commerce market over the next two to three years. The aim is to get more creators to make product-focused content and to make it easier for shoppers to move from watching that content to buying something.
 Content first
 India’s social-commerce market is expected to grow at about 22-24% a year, according to Redseer Strategy Consultants. The company expects its creator-led business to grow faster than the rest and capture a larger share of its overall business.
 The reason, it says, is simple: people are changing how they discover products. Shoppers who interact with social-commerce content have baskets that are more than 40% higher on average, while creator-led content can result in a 10% increase in conversion, according to the company.
 “We see people wanting to be content first. That’s a massive behaviour change,” Lakshminarayan Swaminathan, chief product officer, said in an interview with Mint .
 In the old model, a shopper generally knew what they wanted before opening a shopping app. They searched for a shirt, a pair of shoes or a lipstick and then decided what to buy. The new model starts earlier: a shopper sees something interesting and only then starts thinking about buying it.
 “Rather than only becoming a dukan (shop) where you come once you know that I want this, our job is to give the right inspiration and discovery,” Swaminathan said.
 There is, however, a limit to how far the company wants to go with content. It does not want to become another Instagram or YouTube, where content itself is the main product. Instead, it wants videos and creators to help shoppers discover products and eventually buy them.
 For online fashion companies, the battle may increasingly begin before the search box is opened. The strategy has a parallel in Meesho too, which has also brought creators into its shopping business. In its initial public offering (IPO) documents, the company describes content commerce as a model in which creators use short videos and live streams on Meesho and social-media platforms to help shoppers discover products, while sellers use those creators to promote their merchandise.
 Content commerce generated ₹ 707 crore in net merchandise value in fiscal year 2024-25 (FY25), within two years of its launch, according to the company’s IPO documents. Meesho describes the model as bringing together three groups: creators, sellers and consumers.
 The scale of Myntra’s own business is also growing. The company’s operating revenue rose from ₹ 2,407 crore in FY21 to ₹ 6,043 crore in FY25, according to the company's financials accessed through the business intelligence platform Tofler. Content commerce makes about 10% of this revenue, Mint has learnt from industry insiders.
 Operating profit moved from a loss of ₹ 369 crore to ₹ 442 crore over the same period, while net profit rose to ₹ 548.5 crore in the latest figures available.
 Creator commerce
 The creator-commerce push is no longer a small experiment on the sidelines of the main business. The creator base is growing alongside the platform, too. The platform has nearly 10 million creator sign-ups, with about 500,000 active creators each month, Swaminathan said.
 Shoppers, influencers and other creators have generated more than 20 million pieces of content, while creator video content has grown about 20 times in the past year, he added.
 The activity is not limited to the shopping app. After affiliate features were introduced on Instagram and Facebook, about 650,000 creators became active and generated around 3 million posts that send shoppers back to the platform, Swaminathan said. More than 1 million Instagram users signed up in a month, while Facebook added about 1.3 million sign-ups during the rollout.
 The increase in content is also changing the advertising industry. Mint on 30 September reported that Omnicom Production is building “content factories” as brands demand hundreds or even thousands of versions of campaigns for social media, e-commerce, connected TV and other digital platforms.
 AI is helping companies create and adapt this content faster and at lower cost. Instead of simply using those savings to reduce advertising budgets, brands are using them to make more content in more formats.
 For the fashion platform, that means having more opportunities to put products in front of shoppers before they search for them. Its Glamstream, a video and shopping feature inside the app, has about 7 million users a month, who spend roughly 2.1 million hours on it each month. Gen Z accounts for 52% of its views, Swaminathan said.
 The next step is to bring brands and sellers more directly into this system. The company is testing ways for sellers to find relevant creators, add products to their content, and track what happens afterwards, from views and clicks to sales.
 “What we believe will really strengthen this is bringing the sellers and brands also onto this,” Swaminathan said, adding that it would be a major focus over the next three years.
