Weak execution, order momentum for infrastructure firms in Q2FY27
 Monsoon disruptions, higher input costs and geopolitical tensions weigh on infrastructure firms' Q2FY27 performance, though strong order books provide revenue visibility
 premium 
 Road engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) inflows were just ₹3,100 crore (versus ₹11,100 crore Y-o-Y), with only Ceigall (₹1,800 crore) and Ashoka Buildcon (₹700 crore) securing significant orders | Representative Image
 Devangshu Datta New Delhi 5 min read Last Updated : Oct 08 2026 | 11:42 PM IST
 Listen to This Article
 Trends across the infrastructure space in Q2FY27 appear to be seasonally weak due to the monsoon, with additional challenges arising from geopolitical tensions. Raw material costs are up, and companies with West Asia exposure have additional concerns due to slowdowns and disruptions.
 The monsoon always slows project execution, but the additional challenges may have had more of an impact on civil work. Revenue growth rates may soften quarter-on-quarter (Q-o-Q), while earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) margins are likely to be stable year-on-year (Y-o-Y) at best. The continued policy focus on infrastructure and budgetary allocations supports the outlook, but Q2FY27 activity in roads and construction may be low-key. Bulging order books do give revenue visibility, and there is tender activity across power, transmission, metros, urban infrastructure and data centres.
 In August, NHAI awarded eight road projects, but construction fell 12 per cent Y-o-Y. NHAI plans to award road projects spanning 5,200 kilometres (km), up 66 per cent Y-o-Y, in FY27 while constructing 4,950 km, down 7 per cent Y-o-Y. It missed the awarding target of 4,500 km for FY26. 
 In FY27 year-to-date, awards stand at 329 km, up 69 per cent Y-o-Y. NHAI awarded 3,124 km in FY26. No increase in the budgeted outlay for NHAI in the FY27 Budget leads to concerns since it will need to monetise assets in a big way to avoid debt growth. Year-to-date (YTD) FY27 road construction, at 1,053 km, is down 24 per cent Y-o-Y.
 Order inflows across roads, rail and construction, as announced on the BSE, were ₹22,100 crore (versus ₹74,700 crore in Q2FY26 and ₹57,200 crore in Q1FY27). Transmission and distribution (T&D) players (KEC, Kalpataru) and diversified players (Afcons, NCC, Dilip Buildcon, J Kumar Infra) provided the bulk of Q2FY27 inflows. For many players, H1FY27 inflows are well below FY27 guidance, implying that a sharp increase in orders in H2 will be needed to meet FY27 guidance. Ebitda margins are likely to compress.
 Road engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) inflows were just ₹3,100 crore (versus ₹11,100 crore Y-o-Y), with only Ceigall (₹1,800 crore) and Ashoka Buildcon (₹700 crore) securing significant orders. Construction EPC inflows were ₹1,200 crore, entirely from Capacite. Ahluwalia had no announced orders. Orders from diversified players included Afcons (₹2,800 crore), NCC (₹3,100 crore), Dilip Buildcon (₹2,000 crore) and J Kumar (₹1,000 crore). T&D contractors were led by KEC and Kalpataru. In railways, RVNL secured orders worth ₹1,800 crore. NCC's order book of ₹71,300 crore shows multi-year revenue visibility.
 Among EPC players (excluding L&T), CemIndia Projects could show Y-o-Y revenue growth in the late teens, with execution picking up as delays in the Vadhavan Port project and other monsoon-related disruptions ease. Ebitda could grow Y-o-Y by nearly 30 per cent, with stable Ebitda margins of 10 per cent maintained. Q2FY27 profit after tax (PAT) could grow by 25 per cent Y-o-Y. Order inflows are expected to be strong, with ₹1,240 crore secured in July 2026, a ₹1,000 crore pipeline in L1 status and a longer-term pipeline of ₹90,000 crore. The FY27 inflow target is ₹25,000 crore. Guidance and progress on a proposed qualified institutional placement (QIP) would be keenly watched.
 Power Mech Projects is another potential outperformer, with likely revenue growth above 20 per cent, supported by activity in the mine development and operation segment. Ebitda should also grow by nearly 20 per cent, with margins improving Q-o-Q. The company has secured orders of ₹3,700 crore in H1FY27, which is 31 per cent of its ₹12,000 crore guidance for FY27.
 PSP Projects (PSPPL) may see revenue growth of 30 per cent Y-o-Y on better execution, aided by improved labour availability and progress on projects like the Dharavi redevelopment. Q2FY27 Ebitda is expected to improve Q-o-Q. Order inflows are driven by a bid pipeline, the bulk of which consists of Adani Group projects. The FY27 order inflow guidance target is ₹6,000 crore. The order book is already around ₹13,250 crore, which provides good revenue visibility.
 VA Tech Wabag (VTW) should also see Q2FY27 revenue growth of nearly 20 per cent Y-o-Y, with execution gaining traction in its international EPC portfolio. Ebitda could grow by the mid-teens, with Ebitda margins more or less stable. Order inflows in Q1 were ₹3,430 crore, with 75 per cent from overseas orders, leading to an order book of ₹19,400 crore. Q2 may also see strong order inflows, but West Asia is a key region for large desalination opportunities, and the turmoil there could be a drag.
 J Kumar Infraprojects (JKIL) will probably see revenue growth in the low double digits as execution has improved. Ebitda may grow in single digits, with more or less stable margins. The company's FY27 inflow target is ₹10,000 crore, with an outstanding order book of ₹22,250 crore, which provides strong revenue visibility. The pipeline is over ₹50,000 crore across MSRDC, MMRDA, NHAI, metro rail and flyovers. Management commentary on the pace of execution is a key monitorable. The writer is a New Delhi-based independent journalist.

docs.title: Jefferies’ power play after RBI’s 25 bps rate hike: 7 stocks with up to 53% upside
docs.text: Power companies are now in the spotlight, with a key question - how much will higher borrowing costs affect their earnings? This is after the Reserve Bank of India’s 25 basis point rate hike has put interest-sensitive sectors back in focus. The global investment bank Jefferies published its India utilities outlook on 7 October 2026. Jefferies expects companies with regulated returns, fixed-rate debt and interest-cost pass-through mechanisms to have greater protection. At the same time, Jefferies sees potential in several power stocks after their recent correction. Its top picks are Adani Energy Solutions, JSW Energy and NTPC, with target prices suggesting upside of up to 53%. Jefferies names three top power picks Jefferies in its report added that Adani Energy Solutions, JSW Energy and NTPC remain its preferred stocks in the sector. The global investment bank has a 'Buy' rating on all three. It has set a target price of Rs 2,060 for Adani Energy Solutions, Rs 720 for JSW Energy and Rs 425 for NTPC. These targets imply potential upside of 53%, 45% and 32%, respectively, from their market prices. ALSO READ277% to 1,805% returns: 5 stocks that rose while the market cracked The report also carries Buy ratings on Adani Power, Power Grid, Adani Green Energy and Torrent Power. Their target prices imply upside of 33%, 23%, 29% and 44%, respectively. CompanyRatingTarget Price (Rs )Upside/DownsideNTPCBuyRs 42532% upsideAdani PowerBuyRs 27033% upsidePower GridBuyRs 31523% upsideAdani Green EnergyBuyRs 1,69529% upsideTata PowerUnpfRs 3355% downsideAdani Energy SolutionsBuyRs 2,06053% upsideJSW EnergyBuyRs 72045% upsideTorrent PowerBuyRs 1,78044% upsideIndian Energy Exchange (IEX)UnpfRs 1005% downside Why higher rates may not hurt all stocks equally? As per the Jefferies report, the Reserve Bank of India’s 25 basis point rate hike to 5.5% was largely expected. However, the change in stance has raised expectations of further rate increases. “Power companies have some protection against hikes between regulated equity, fixed rate loans and lower rate hike pass through,” the report noted. NTPC, Power Grid and Adani Energy Solutions are expected to see a relatively limited impact on earnings from higher rates. According to Jefferies, NTPC and Power Grid have 36-57% of their loans on a fixed-rate basis. More than 70% of their gross block is also under regulated returns, where interest costs can be passed through. For Adani Energy Solutions, more than 65% of loans are fixed-rate, which provides another layer of protection. Adani Green faces a bigger rate risk Adani Green Energy has relatively high leverage, with net debt-to-equity at around 6.5-6.6 times. Jefferies expects Adani Green to see more than a 15% impact on earnings per share from a 100 basis point rise in rates. However, the brokerage noted that longer-tenure fixed-rate overseas loans and refinancing after projects become operational could reduce the impact. ALSO READSensex target 89,000 by June 2027: Why Morgan Stanley sees 24% upside led by 10 stocks Could power shortages return? Power demand has risen 10% year-on-year so far in 2026, while generation increased 13% year-on-year in September. Jefferies expects the possibility of power shortages returning in the coming months to remain an important factor for the sector. “15-30% stock price correction from peak – shortages could reappear in 4-5 months,” the report added. Jefferies expects higher merchant power prices to potentially offset some of the interest-rate impact on JSW Energy. It also sees scope for higher merchant tariffs to improve the trading business of Adani Energy Solutions. Recent correction creates stock-specific opportunities According to the Jefferies report, the power sector remains constructive despite the recent correction in several stocks. Jefferies believes the decline from peak levels over the past five to six months has created stock-specific opportunities rather than a broad sector-level concern. “We remain constructive on the power sector overall and believe the recent correction in stocks from peak levels in the last 5-6 months is a stock-specific buying opportunity,” the report added. docs.title: 5 auto sector picks by Citi ahead of festive season, with 31% to 49% upside potential
docs.text: Citi expects the festive season to be a key test for India’s auto sector as companies enter the second half of FY27 with a tougher year-on-year base and rising input costs. Vehicle volumes have remained healthy so far, but higher steel, copper, plastics and rubber prices are expected to keep pressure on gross margins. Recent price hikes, better product mix and operating leverage could partly offset the cost burden, with Maruti Suzuki, Eicher Motors and Mahindra & Mahindra remaining Citi’s top picks. The brokerage will be watching retail sales, enquiries, booking momentum, dealer inventory and order backlogs during the festive period. Rural demand will also be important for tractors and entry-level motorcycles and cars, particularly after a weak monsoon. Citi on Mahindra & Mahindra: 'Buy' Citi has given a ‘Buy’ rating to Mahindra & Mahindra with a target price of Rs 4,260, indicating an upside of 49%. The brokerage expects strong growth in passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles and three-wheelers to support the auto business, although a seasonal decline in tractor volumes and higher commodity costs are likely to weigh on margins. Citi estimates total vehicle volumes to rise 15.7% year-on-year in the September quarter. Passenger vehicle volumes are expected to grow 26%, commercial vehicle volumes 17.8% and three-wheeler volumes 38.7%, while tractor volumes are estimated to decline 5.6%. ALSO READBeyond warships: 2 stocks riding India’s Rs 69,725 cr small-shipbuilding push The brokerage said, "We pencil in 90bps QoQ gross margin decline due to weaker mix (seasonal decline in tractor volumes) and elevated commodity cost pressures. We will watch out for any change in guidance on tractor volumes. (currently mid-single digit)." Citi expects revenue to rise 26.7% year-on-year in the quarter, while earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation are estimated to decline 1.8% because of margin pressure. Citi on Maruti Suzuki: 'Buy' Citi has given a ‘Buy’ rating to Maruti Suzuki with a target price of Rs 16,500, indicating an upside of 42%. Maruti Suzuki remains one of Citi’s preferred auto names, with strong volume growth expected to support the business despite higher commodity costs. docs.title: PB Fintech down 45% since IRDAI proposal; Nomura slashes target, FY28 PAT estimates by 72%
docs.text: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority’s proposed commission limits are expected to hurt the industry and one company, PB Fintech, seems to get the worst of it. The share price of PB Fintech has already declined nearly 45% in the last few weeks. Japanese brokerage Nomura has now cut its target price for the stock by 31% to Rs 1,100 apiece and has maintained its ‘Neutral’ rating. This implies an upside of around 9% from the stock’s current price of Rs 1,012 apiece. The brokerage has revised its financial model for PB Fintech as it trims POSP (point of sales person) business’ premiums assuming the company exits the segment, while keeping PolicyBazaar, Dubai, and the corporate segment untouched. It has revised take rates according to the proposed commission caps, and trimmed total expenses for FY28 and FY29 by 40% and 48%, respectively. ALSO READ277% to 1,805% returns: 5 stocks that rose while the market cracked Nomura on PB Fintech: Base case scenario The changes to the financial model lead to a 13% cut to insurance premium for FY28 and 72% cut to PB Fintech’s net profit estimate. For FY29, Nomura expects a 19% cut to insurance premium and 51% cut to net profit. The brokerage expects earnings before interest, tax, depreciation, and amortisation (EBITDA) margin to decline to 7.9% in FY28 and then to recover to 18.2% in FY29. “We now expect a FY26-50F revenue CAGR in discounted cash flow (DCF) of 13.2% vs 15.1% earlier,” Nomura said. Nomura on PB Fintech: If commission caps are raised by 2pp “PB Fintech has been arguing that its support to customers at the time of hospital discharge is a key offering that improves customer experience. Thus, in our first scenario (S1) we assume a 2pp (percentage point) higher commission cap vs what has been proposed currently for the health insurance segment. We make no other changes in our S1 vs our base case,” Nomura said. In such a scenario, Nomura projected a 3 percentage point increase in its revenue estimate and 37% rise in net profit estimate for FY28, against its base case. For FY29, a 4 percentage point increase in revenue estimate and 19% rise in net profit estimate is seen, compared with the brokerage’s base case. Its revenue CAGR estimate over FY26 to FY50 will increase by 40 basis points against the base case. Nomura on PB Fintech: If PolicyBazaar sells traditional savings products The fintech company is looking at multiple new product segments. In Nomura’s second scenario, it assumes a new savings product to form 0.5-1.1% of its total premium mix over FY28 and FY29. “Further, we expect a FY26-50F revenue CAGR to lift by 80bp vs our base case. We make no other changes to our S2 vs our base case,” it said. ALSO READNomura initiates coverage on this optical cable play: Datacentre capex to fuel 35% rally? “This leads to a 5-6pp higher net profit in S2 vs our base case (for FY28-29F). docs.title: Oil spikes 4%: Brent tops $104 as Gulf Hurricane shut-ins and Iran risks tighten supply
docs.text: Crude oil futures jumped 4% on Thursday as supply disruptions caused by prolonged Middle East tensions, coupled with the US halt in production due to a storm in the Gulf of Mexico, added to the price rise. The December contract for Brent crude futures jumped 4% above the $104/bbl mark, while the US contract, West Texas Intermediate, was up 3.85% near the $92/bbl level. Attacks on tankers sailing through the waterway route- the Strait of Hormuz- hit their highest mark in a single week since the beginning of the West Asia conflict, Reuters reported, citing maritime security sources. This added to market fear of further supply disruptions. US crude exports affected from hurricane Tropical Storm Isaias prompted Gulf of Mexico producers to shut down a large chunk of offshore production, which accounts for nearly 15% of crude imported to the US annually. As per the Marine Minerals Administration, producers halted 511,000 bpd due to the Atlantic hurricane. “With oil prices already high, the production cuts are steep enough to affect markets, though other Gulf hurricanes have caused larger disruptions, “ ABC News quoted Jim Burkhard, global head of crude oil market research for S&P Global Energy, as saying. He added that the possibility of Isaias striking as a powerful storm near refineries will add to further market tensions. ALSO READ7 reasons why the market is falling today: Nifty below 22,300, Sensex slides over 1,000 points Crude prices far from normalisation Commenting on the rise in oil prices, Ole Hansen, head of commodity strategy at Saxo Bank, said in a social media post that crude rose following the flare-up in US-Iran tensions. He added that the White House has reportedly asked the Pentagon to prepare possible military strike plans in the Middle East. These, combined with the halt of US production due to the storm in the Gulf of Mexico, added to the price rise. He noted that all of these developments combined showcase that oil markets remain far from normalisation. “Crude continues to be shipped at exceptionally high cost, while curtailed fuel exports are keeping product markets tight. Gasoil - the key pricing benchmark for diesel, jet fuel, marine and heating fuels - has climbed back above $191 per barrel,” Hansen added.

docs.title: Can Physicswallah outgrow JEE/NEET? Motilal sees 43% upside on K-12, state board push
docs.text: The share price of Physicswallah is in focus today, October 8, after domestic brokerage house Motilal Oswal reiterated its ‘Buy’ recommendation on Physicswallah and set a target price of Rs 200. This implies an upside of nearly 43% from the stock’s current price of Rs 140 (as of 11 am October 8). The brokerage engaged with the top management of Physicswallah, with discussions around online growth drivers, the K-12 opportunity, the path to offline profitability, and capital allocation. Motilal Oswal believes multiple growth legs have emerged which can help the company achieve a 30% compounded annual growth rate (CAGR) for its online business in the next 3-4 years, with a clear path towards sustained earnings before interest, tax, depreciation, and amortisation (EBITDA) improvement over the same period. “The team highlighted that online growth is no longer tied to JEE/NEET, as newer categories, including K-12 and state boards, scale at high margins. Offline is expected to near break-even in FY27, and admissions for the year are already closed. For online, we expect pre-IND AS EBITDA margins to remain in the 30-35% range over the next 4-5 years, with the potential to reach upwards of 40% over the medium term,” the brokerage said. ALSO READ277% to 1,805% returns: 5 stocks that rose while the market cracked Motilal Oswal on Physicswallah: Growth beyond JEE/NEET The online K-12 penetration remains at only around 0.5% of the 165 million student total addressable market. The company’s management highlighted that K-12 extends the student lifetime on the platform to 15-18 years from around 2 years in test preparation. It expects the segment to eventually outgrow test preparation. Curious Junior, the company’s premium after-school offering at Rs 24,000 a year, has reached around 50,000 students and Rs 125 crore of collections in 18 months, “The business should near break-even this year after a loss in FY26. Management believes it could eventually match test prep in scale,” the brokerage said. Moreover, state boards are scaling rapidly, with 4 lakh students across six states within 18 months of launch. The addressable base of 6 crore students compares with 20 lakh CBSE exam takers every year. “Margins are 27% today, and management expects them to exceed JEE/NEET at maturity, given the lower faculty costs. Six more states, new streams, and foundation courses are in the pipeline,” it added. Motilal Oswal on Physicswallah: Offline biz near break even in FY27 The offline pre-IND AS EBITDA margin expanded to -10% in FY26 from -19% in FY25 and is expected to reach -2% to -3% in FY27. “The core Vidyapeeth and Pathshaala network, which makes up ~70% of offline, is already profitable. The remaining drag comes from newer categories such as government exams, CA, and MBA, as well as acquired subsidiaries,” Motilal said. Physicswallah has deliberately slowed expansion as it will add only 25-30 centers in FY27 until profitability is proven. Offline expansion in GATE, CA, and UPSC has been halted as these markets shift online. The company’s management has guided for a 20-22% offline growth with a steady state margin of 15%. ALSO READBernstein upgrades IEX: Sees delay in market coupling lowering near-term pressures Motilal Oswal on Physicswallah: Artificial intelligence The company’s management believes AI tools are largely used for homework answers rather than structured learnings. “AI is already deeply embedded in the product. 90% of student doubts are now resolved by AI, with turnaround cut from 24-48 hours to minutes. Physicswallah runs its own fine-tuned small language models (Aryabhatta) and routes only complex queries to frontier models, which keeps inference costs low,” Motilal said. Motilal Oswal on Physicswallah: Valuations The brokerage has assigned a 50 times FY28 estimated enterprise value-to-EBITDA ratio to Physicswallah, reflecting its market leadership, structurally superior unit economics, and scalable technology platform. Its offline business is valued at 15 times FY28 estimated enterprise value-to-EBITDA ratio. Motilal Oswal on Physicswallah: New growth legs to drive performance Physicswallah has a near-monopoly in the online test preparation market, and is currently expanding to K-12 and state boards. Motilal Oswal remains bullish on the stock. The company’s offline business is also expected to near break even in FY27. docs.text: Nuvama Institutional Equities has initiated coverage on Sagility, a pure-play US healthcare business process management company, which serves payers and providers. This implies a nearly 38% upside from the stock’s closing price of Rs 43.49 apiece on Thursday. “Its long-standing client relationships, broadening capabilities and growing presence in the mid-market payers provide multiple avenues to expand wallet share. We believe Sagility is well placed to benefit from rising healthcare outsourcing, supported by deep domain expertise, a recurring revenue base and an evolving AI-led delivery model,” Nuvama said. ALSO READBeyond warships: 2 stocks riding India’s Rs 69,725 cr small-shipbuilding push Nuvama on Sagility: Deep relationship with payers The company’s payer-led model is a key differentiating factor, with capabilities spanning claims, clinical management, payment integrity, and member and provider lifecycle management. Sagility’s top five client relationships average around 18 years with overall retention at 97%, underpinning a sticky revenue base. It is also diversifying clients, as top-five concentration fell to 70.4% in FY26 from 80.6% in FY23. Client groups worth over $20 million has also risen to nine from four. Nuvama on Sagility: Cross-selling, outsourcing tailwinds Spending on healthcare operations in the US is expected to rise to $259 billion by 2028 from $201 billion in 2023, with outsourced operations growth outstripping in-house spending growth. “Sagility’s payer-heavy mix provides exposure to the larger outsourcing pool while its expanding provider presence adds exposure to a faster growing segment,” Nuvama said. The BroadPath and CareSeed acquisitions have widened the client base, Devlin Consulting, Inc. acquisition and BirchAI expanded the capability set, creating a two-way cross-sell opportunity across legacy and acquired accounts. “We envisage AI as a net opportunity over time with the model shifting from effort-based revenue towards productivity-led growth, managed and outcome based engagements helping offset potential AI-led revenue deflation and expanding the TAM,” the brokerage added. Nuvama on Sagility: Attractive valuations leaves re-rating room Nuvama reckons Sagility’s current valuation, at 15 times FY28 price-to-earnings, as “highly attractive”. The brokerage expects Sagility’s revenue, in dollars, to increase 13% on a compounded annual growth rate (CAGR) basis over FY26 to FY29. ALSO READCan Physicswallah outgrow JEE/NEET? Motilal sees 43% upside on K-12, state board push It sees adjusted earnings per share grow 19% on a CAGR over the same period and expects earnings before interest, tax, depreciation, and amortisation (EBITDA) margins to be resilient at 24%-25%. Healthy cash generation and a largely debt-free balance sheet by FY27 should also support returns. Nuvama on Sagility: Key risks The brokerage said high client concentration, promoter overhang and high exposure to the US healthcare industry are key risks to the company’s growth. It also sees the AI-led revenue deflation, currency, and macro sensitivity as other major risk factors. Nuvama on Sagility: Well placed to benefit from healthcare outsourcing Sagility’s long-standing client relationships, along with diversification efforts provide avenues to expand revenue. The company’s valuations are highly attractive, leaving room for re-rating. US healthcare expansion and cross-selling opportunities to unlock new growth opportunities. docs.title: SEBI introduces a credit risk-o-meter for debt securities
docs.text: Securities and exchange board of India (SEBI) introduced a credit risk-o-meter for debt securities on Wednesday aimed to assist investors in assessing credit risk through colour-coded visualization prior to investing. The disclosure of risk-o-meter will be applicable to all listed and proposed to be listed issuances of non-convertible securities (NCS), commercial papers (CPs), securitized debt instruments (SDIs), security receipts (SRs) and structured debt /market-linked debentures (MLDs), whether issued by way of public issue or private placement. ALSO READStocks to watch for October 8: Senco Gold, Jubilant FoodWorks, Fino Payments, and more The new risk-o-meter will have to be mandatorily included in offer document, abridged prospectus, private placement memorandum, all ads of issuer and online bond platform provider (OBPPs) and their web and mobile platforms. The regulator has asked the exchanges and depositories to put in place necessary systems and processes to implement the measure within the next 45 days. Further, the regulator also exempted issuers issuing debt securities or non-convertible redeemable preference shares on a private placement basis from the requirement of hiring a merchant banker. The regulator had proposed the same in its consultation paper in August 2026. The exemption will only be applicable if the issuer is registered or regulated by a financial sector regulator in India (like SEBI, RBI, IRDAI or PFRDA) or the issuer is listed in any segment on any of the recognized stock exchange for a period of at least one year with no pending fines or penalties. The issuer must also not have defaulted in the last three financial years and the current financial year on any payments due in respect to the securities like repayment, interest, dividend. The exemption will be applicable only for unsubordinated or senior debt securities rated AA- or above secured by a first or pari-passu charge on the identifiable assets of the issuer. For public issuers, however, the debt securities can be secured or unsecured. If a debt security has multiple ratings, the lowest rating will be considered for determining eligibility for exemption. The regulator also increased the maximum number of international securities identification numbers (ISINs) maturing in a financial year for issuance of debt securities on a private placement basis from 14 to 17 with further six ISINs available for issuance of capital gains tax debt securities by authorized issuers. A maximum of 12 of these 17 ISINs will be allowed for the issuance of plain vanilla secured and unsecured debt securities with an aggregate upper limit of Rs 15,000 crore across issuances. ALSO READUS 10-year Treasury yield hits 5.32%: What is driving the rise? For each additional issuance of Rs 3,000 crore, one additional ISIN may be permitted to mature in the same financial year. A maximum of five ISINs maturing per financial year shall be allowed for structured debt securities, market-linked debt securities, floating rate bonds (FRBs), zero coupon bonds (ZCBs), and debt capital instruments (Tier II bonds). For issuers with only structured/market linked debt securities/FRBs/ZCBs/debt capital instruments (Tier II bonds), the upper limit will be of 12 ISINs in a financial year. Government of India serviced or extra budgetary resources (EBR) bonds, ESG debt securities will be excluded from calculating the ISIN limits.

docs.title: Beyond warships: 2 stocks riding India’s Rs 69,725 cr small-shipbuilding push
docs.text: There is no denying that the investment opportunity around the naval defence build up gets almost all the attention. But perhaps, there is an alternate maritime capex opportunity that may be smaller than a destroyer and closer to the port - but exciting nevertheless. Tugs, workboats and pilot boats, all smaller boats in comparison, are directly tied to vessel handling, harbour operations, pilotage and offshore support, making port traffic and shipbuilding capacity relevant demand indicators. India’s ports handled more than 1.59 billion tonnes of cargo in FY2024-25. Major ports alone handled 915.17 MT in FY26, registering 7.06% year-on-year growth and surpassing their 904 MT target. The policy backdrop has also changed materially. Under the Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Policy, 288 contracts covering 456 vessels worth ₹19,748 crore had received in-principle approval by March 2026, with tugs specifically included among the eligible vessel categories. The government has since approved a ₹69,725-crore shipbuilding package, including ₹24,736 crore for the Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Scheme, ₹25,000 crore for the Maritime Development Fund and ₹19,989 crore for the Shipbuilding Development Scheme. The latter aims to expand India's shipbuilding capacity to 4.5 million gross tonnes annually. FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now For harbour craft, this matters because these vessels are generally smaller, have shorter construction cycles and serve recurring port and coastal requirements. Against this backdrop, two listed names come into focus: Knowledge Marine & Engineering Works and Cochin Shipyard. #1 Knowledge Marine & Engineering Works: The Higher-Purity Harbour-Craft Bet Knowledge Marine & Engineering Works Limited (KMEW) operates across port ancillary crafts, shipbuilding and repair, and dredging. Its vessel business covers conventional tugs, hybrid tugs, Green Tug Transition Programme (GTTP) tugs, pilot boats, speed patrol boats, mooring boats, service boats and multi-utility workboats. Its shipbuilding activity includes construction of small and specialised marine crafts, while the company also undertakes repair and refit of marine vessels. Its broader port-services capabilities include hydrographic surveys, pilotage and patrolling. Q1 FY27 Shows Where The Earnings Are Actually Coming From KMEW delivered a sharp improvement in Q1 FY27, with consolidated revenue from operations rising to ₹115.41 crore, up 138.2% YoY and 70.7% QoQ. Consolidated profit after tax (PAT) rose to ₹62.75 crore from ₹11.08 crore in Q1 FY26 and ₹23.53 crore in Q4 FY26. However, the 54.4% Q1 PAT margin should not be treated as a sustainable run-rate. Management has indicated a more normal operating-margin range of 35-40%, with the quarter benefiting from unusually strong dredging execution. The biggest change was the business mix. Dredging and ancillary services generated ₹104.41 crore of segment revenue in Q1 FY27, up 286.9% YoY and 52.8% QoQ. Shipbuilding contributed ₹21.22 crore versus zero in Q1 FY26 and ₹11.26 crore in Q4 FY26, with earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) of ₹3.41 crore. This matters for the maritime-capex thesis because KMEW's current earnings are still being driven primarily by dredging rather than by the construction of tugs and workboats. The shipbuilding opportunity is therefore a forward-looking growth engine, not yet the dominant earnings contributor. Strong Order Book But Its Composition Matters More As per the August 2026 earnings call, KMEW had an order book of over ₹1,300 crore, of which dredging was ₹240 crore, charter and hire was ₹850 crore and shipbuilding was ₹240 crore. The company also had an additional ₹200-crore inter-company order book placed with Knowledge Shipyard for Green Tugs and patrol boats. The company had 10 accommodation boats, 10 work boats, four cutter-suction dredgers, two 60-tonne bollard-pull green tugs and 10 hybrid-electric passenger ferries under its broader ongoing project portfolio. Separately, it was building three tugs and two boats for captive use and about 42 vessels for third parties. The order-book mix therefore shows that the immediate earnings base remains broader than shipbuilding, even as vessel construction becomes an increasingly important future growth driver. Saphale Could Change The Earnings Mix KMEW is undertaking roughly ₹1,000 crore of capex over the next 1.5 years, with about ₹250 crore earmarked for green tugs and green vessels, ₹450 crore for dredging and the balance for shipyard and shipbuilding operations. Phase I of the Saphale shipyard is expected to become operational by the end of FY27, with capacity for 14 vessels annually in Phase I and 18 vessels after completion of all phases. This is arguably the most important structural change in KMEW's investment case. The company is moving from owning and chartering marine assets towards building a dedicated manufacturing platform that can support a larger shipbuilding order pipeline. Management has indicated that the yard is already being positioned for orders over the next two financial years. It is therefore important to track order intake, vessel values, yard utilisation and execution margins as the Saphale facility ramps up. ₹1,000 Crore Capex Makes Funding A Key Monitor Debt remains an important investor monitor. By March 2026, consolidated borrowings stood at about ₹222.1 crore against cash and cash equivalents of ₹73.6 crore, implying net borrowings of roughly ₹148.4 crore. The debt to equity is at 0.39x. FY26 operating cash flow was negative at ₹200.4 crore, largely reflecting substantial deployment into other financial assets, while investing cash outflow was ₹104.4 crore, including ₹119.1 crore of property, plant and equipment purchases. docs.title: Defence capex up 37%: Kotak sees strong Q2 growth for Solar, BEL & HAL on Rs 1.6 tn AoNs
docs.text: India’s defence spending is moving at a faster pace. The key question is whether this spending will translate into fresh orders and revenue growth for listed companies. According to the Kotak brokerage report dated October 4, 2026, defence capital expenditure rose 37% year-on-year in the first five months of FY26-27. Approvals under Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) have already crossed Rs 1.6 trillion this year. Kotak believes the pipeline remains strong. However, the timing of large defence orders will be crucial. The brokerage expects Bharat Electronics, Hindustan Aeronautics and Solar Industries to report healthy growth in the September quarter. For shipbuilders such as Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders and Cochin Shipyard, fresh orders remain important. Defence spending sets the backdrop The government’s defence spending continues to support the sector. As per the brokerage report, only around 31% of the full-year defence capital expenditure budget had been used during the period, suggesting that spending could pick up in the second half. ALSO READBeyond warships: 2 stocks riding India’s Rs 69,725 cr small-shipbuilding push Kotak report added, “Defence capex spending remains healthy in FY2027, with the central government’s defense capital expenditure spend growing at 37% yoy in the first five months of 2027, although only 31% of the FY2207 budget estimate has been utilized so far, indicating a stronger spending pace is likely in the second half of the year.” The order pipeline is another key factor. Cumulative AoN approvals since FY23-24 have crossed Rs 18 trillion. These approvals cover areas such as radars, electronic warfare systems, helicopters, naval platforms and other defence equipment. But approvals are not the same as orders. Big orders could decide the next phase According to Kotak, several large programmes are waiting for Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS) clearance. These include the Quick Reaction Surface-to-Air Missile (QRSAM) programme worth around Rs 30,000, Project-75 India (P75I) submarines, Next Generation Corvettes and a survey vessel order for Cochin Shipyard. The report noted, “While AoNs typically convert into contracts with a 1-2-year lag, the current pipeline provides strong order inflow visibility reinforcing long-term growth visibility for the sector.” For Bharat Electronics, the QRSAM order is a major monitorable. The company is expected to report around 16% year-on-year revenue growth in the second quarter of FY26-27. BEL, HAL and Solar Industries in focus Bharat Electronics is expected to see better margins, while investor attention could remain on order conversion. Its year-to-date order inflows are down 44% year-on-year, making new awards important for future visibility. ALSO READPB Fintech down 45% since IRDAI proposal; Nomura slashes target, FY28 PAT estimates by 72% Hindustan Aeronautics is expected to post around 14% year-on-year revenue growth to Rs 7,560 crore. According to the brokerage report, deliveries of Tejas trainers, HTT-40 trainers and Dhruv Next Generation helicopters should support the quarter. “Investor focus is likely to remain on the pace of GE engine supplies (three deliveries in August) and the timely resolution of Tejas Mk1A missile integration issues, which remain critical for accelerating deliveries and sustaining growth visibility,” the report noted. Solar Industries could record the sharpest growth among the key defence names. Kotak expects revenue to rise around 47% year-on-year, helped by a 120% jump in defence revenue. What about shipbuilders and aerospace? Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders could see flat revenue, while Cochin Shipyard is expected to grow around 11% year-on-year. For both, fresh orders will determine how quickly the order book gets replenished. In aerospace and precision engineering, Aequs stands out for its expected 56% revenue growth. The brokerage expects aerospace and consumer businesses to drive the performance. INDO-MIM, meanwhile, is expected to deliver steady sequential growth. However, margins could depend on the share of higher-margin defence and medical businesses. docs.title: Jio IPO: What it means for RIL shareholders & 4 key factors to watch
docs.text: For years, Jio has sat quietly inside the Reliance empire, its worth known only through estimates and boardroom numbers. That is about to change. Jio Platforms IPO has already got the SEBI nod and recent buzz indicates that the issue could be launched in the next few weeks. Though there is no official announcement yet, the issue size is likely to be nearly Rs 37,700 crore. For shareholders of Reliance Industries (RIL), which owns about 66.4% of Jio, this is more than a headline. What could change for Reliance Industries after the Jio listing? Here’s a closer look at what investors need to watch. Jio could get a valuation of Rs 11 lakh crore Motilal Oswal in its report dated October 6, 2026 estimates that Jio Platforms could command an equity valuation of around Rs 11 lakh crore. This is broadly in line with the brokerage’s own valuation of Rs 11.2 lakh crore. At this valuation, Jio Platform would trade at around 12 times estimated FY28 enterprise value to earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EV/EBITDA). That valuation matters for RIL because the parent company owns around 66.4% of Jio Platforms. ALSO READJio IPO countdown: Motilal sees Rs 11 lk cr valuation; may trigger Airtel & RIL re-rating Will RIL face a holding company discount? This is something interesting to watch. Once Jio becomes a separately listed company, investors could argue that RIL’s stake in Jio platform should not be valued at the same price as Jio platform itself. A holding company discount is generally applied when investors value a parent company’s stake in another listed business. Motilal Oswal, however, believes this concern may already be reflected in RIL’s share price. The brokerage estimates that RIL is already factoring in an 18–36% holding company discount on its Jio stake, depending on the valuation multiple assumed for Reliance Retail Ventures (RRVL). Could investors move from RIL to Jio? Some investors may want direct exposure to Jio after its listing instead of owning Jio indirectly through RIL. Could that reduce demand for RIL? Motilal Oswal believes the concern is limited because Jio Platform is expected to have an initial free float of only around 3%. That means only a small portion of Jio would initially be available for public trading. The brokerage therefore believes a significant shift in telecom-sector allocations from RIL or Bharti Airtel to JPL may be overstated. RIL will still have more than Jio For RIL shareholders, the company’s story does not end with Jio. RIL will continue to have exposure to retail and its integrated energy businesses. It also has businesses and growth opportunities in areas such as new energy, data centres, artificial intelligence and fast-moving consumer goods. Another key factor to watch is what can drive RIL after Jio gets listed? Tariff hikes could become another trigger Motilal Oswal report also pointed to telecom pricing. The brokerage noted that the delay in tariff hikes has been one reason behind the weaker performance of both RIL and Bharti Airtel. It expects the case for a tariff increase to strengthen after the Jio IPO and Vodafone Idea’s expected fundraise. Motilal Oswal has built in a smartphone tariff hike of around 15% in December 2026. It expects this to support around 15% annualised growth in EBITDA over FY26–29. ALSO READMukesh Ambani-led Jio Platforms IPO likely by October 21: Reuters For RIL shareholders, higher Jio tariffs could therefore become important because stronger telecom earnings could support the value of RIL’s remaining stake in JPL. What should RIL shareholders watch? The Jio IPO could give the market a clearer price for one of RIL’s biggest businesses. But the impact on RIL will depend on what happens to the holding company discount and how investors value the rest of the conglomerate. So, for RIL shareholders, the Jio IPO is not simply about Jio getting listed. It is about whether a separate valuation for Jio can make RIL a candidate for potential rerating. docs.title: Why Jefferies prefers large caps as RBI hikes rates; favours HDFC Bank, RIL, Airtel
docs.text: The Reserve Bank of India has begun a new rate hike cycle, and Jefferies expects the move to put further pressure on equity valuations, particularly after the benchmark’s price-to-earnings multiple has already contracted in recent months. The global investment banking firm now expects another 50-75 basis points of rate increases, taking cumulative tightening in the current cycle to about 100 basis points. Jefferies said the RBI’s 25-basis-point increase in the repo rate to 5.50% was widely expected, but the change in monetary policy stance from ‘neutral’ to ‘calibrated tightening’ points to a longer period of tighter financial conditions. Against this backdrop, the brokerage prefers large-cap stocks, with large banks, Reliance Industries, Bharti Airtel and power utilities among its preferred areas. Mahesh Nandurkar, Abhinav Sinha, Priyank Shah and Aditi Singla of Jefferies said, “The RBI's 25bps hike to benchmark rates was as anticipated; however, the shift in stance to 'caliberated tightening' has raised worries of a prolonged tightening cycle. RBI raised estimates on both growth and CPI, indicating strong nominal GDP growth, which should support corporate earnings.” Inflation is giving the RBI reason to keep tightening The Monetary Policy Committee raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% on October 7 after keeping rates unchanged for nine months. The decision was unanimous, while the change in stance to calibrated tightening was backed by four of the six members. Jefferies now expects the RBI to raise rates at the upper end of its earlier 50-100 basis-point expectation. With 25 basis points already delivered, the brokerage sees another 50-75 basis points of increases in the current cycle. The inflation outlook has also worsened. Jefferies has raised its FY27 headline consumer price inflation forecast by 20 basis points to 5.2%, while its core inflation forecast has moved to 4.4% from 4.3%. The brokerage expects headline inflation to reach 5.8% over the next three quarters, with the December 2026 quarter forecast at 6%. “A combination of resurging Crude Oil prices and weak monsoon rainfall has driven a 0.2ppt increase in FY27E CPI estimates to 5.2%, with Core-CPI forecasted to rise to 4.4% (prev. 4.3%) vs. RBI target of 4.0%. The inflation outlook has been deemed to be "not benign" as CPI is now expected to surge to 5.8% over the next 3 qtrs,” Jefferies said. ALSO READBernstein upgrades IEX: Sees delay in market coupling lowering near-term pressures Growth is strong enough to absorb higher rates for now The RBI has raised its FY27 real gross domestic product growth forecast by 40 basis points to 7.1%, following 7.8% growth in the June 2026 quarter and sustained strength in economic indicators. Jefferies also pointed to strong bank credit growth. Credit growth has reached 18.1% year-on-year, while deposit growth has risen to 17.3%, with foreign currency non-resident deposit flows helping deposits catch up. The banking system was also carrying surplus liquidity of Rs 4.9 lakh crore, according to the report. “With the 1QFY27 (Jun'qtr) GDP growth coming in at 7.8%, and reasonably strong economic datapoints sustaining (link), the RBI has raised the FY27 GDP est. by 0.4ppt to 7.1%. The governor also noted the nearly all-time high bank credit growth sustaining near the current high-teen levels,” Jefferies said. The brokerage expects the present tightening cycle to remain smaller than the one seen in 2022. The RBI raised rates by 250 basis points in that episode following policy normalisation and a surge in crude oil and inflation. Jefferies now expects cumulative tightening of about 100 basis points in the current cycle, which would take the repo rate to about 6.25%. With the RBI’s June 2027 quarter inflation forecast at 5.6%, the brokerage expects real policy rates to become substantially positive. Why Jefferies is moving towards large caps Higher rates have historically been accompanied by valuation compression, and Jefferies expects that pattern to remain relevant during the current tightening cycle. ALSO READBeyond warships: 2 stocks riding India’s Rs 69,725 cr small-shipbuilding push The brokerage said the MSCI India forward price-to-earnings multiple fell 22% from its January 2022 peak to June 2022 as the RBI accelerated rate increases. During the narrower 50-basis-point tightening cycle in 2018, the compression was about 7%. Since August 2026, MSCI India’s price-to-earnings multiple has already fallen about 8%. “Experience with prior rate-hike cycles shows a correlation between the quantum of tightening vs. valuation compression. MSCI India P/E compressed by 22% from peak in Jan'22 to Jun'22 as the RBI commenced an accelerated rate tightening. Earlier, in a narrower (50bps) 2018 rate-hike cycle, MSCI India P/E compression was ~7%,” Jefferies said. The valuation gap is also working in favour of larger companies. Jefferies’ analysis shows that the Nifty 100 is trading at a 30% valuation discount to the Nifty Midcap 150, compared with a 10-year average discount of 20%. At the same time, the earnings growth gap between the two segments is expected to narrow. Jefferies’ estimates show two-year earnings growth of 14% for the Nifty 100 over FY26-FY28, compared with 20% for the Nifty Midcap 150. Large banks, Reliance Industries and Bharti Airtel lead preferred list Jefferies has retained an overweight stance on financials, energy, telecom, metals, power and utilities, and real estate in its model portfolio. docs.title: Bernstein upgrades IEX: Sees delay in market coupling lowering near-term pressures
docs.text: Bernstein has upgraded Indian Energy Exchange Ltd. to ‘Market-Perform’ from ‘Underperform’, saying the expected delay in market coupling gives the exchange more time before its market share and transaction charges come under pressure. The brokerage, however, continues to expect market coupling to eventually reduce Indian Energy Exchange’s market share and transaction charges. Bernstein has pushed its expected market coupling timeline back by about a year, citing legal challenges and operational hurdles. It now expects coupling in the day-ahead market by the end of FY28 and in the real-time market by the end of FY29. The brokerage has also cut its target price to Rs 110 from Rs 115, with the new target implying 5% upside based on the price cited in its report. The Bernstein analysts stated that the central part of their thesis on Indian Energy Exchange remains unchanged. “Our thesis remains intact -we think market coupling is inevitable, and so is market share loss and transaction charge softening. In our assessment the stock seems fairly priced for our base case outcome of these events, and hence we are upgrading to Market-Perform.” Legal and operational hurdles give IEX more time Bernstein said market coupling is likely to take longer than previously expected because Indian Energy Exchange is likely to challenge the final regulation and several operational issues still need to be addressed. The brokerage expects the exchange to challenge the final Central Electricity Regulatory Commission regulation in higher forums. It also pointed to Grid India’s limited experience in price discovery, software alignment across the three exchanges and the more complicated task of clearing trades when buy and sell orders are placed on different exchanges. “Apart from legal hurdles (it is highly likely that IEX will challenge the final CERC regulation on market coupling in higher forums). There are operational challenges in market coupling as well: Grid India’s limited expertise in price discovery, software alignment across the 3 exchanges and more importantly clearing of trades across exchanges,” Bernstein said. “All these are addressable points in our view, but will take time to implement.” Bernstein has therefore moved its expected timeline for day-ahead market coupling to the end of FY28 from early FY28 earlier. For the real-time market, it now expects implementation by the end of FY29. The brokerage has also delayed its assumptions on transaction charge reductions in line with the revised coupling schedule. Its model now assumes a more gradual moderation in charges, with the transaction fee reaching 3 paise per unit by FY32. New power products could lift exchange volumes over time While the near-term volume outlook has weakened, Bernstein expects power exchanges to gain a larger share of electricity traded in India over the medium to long term. The brokerage said the formalisation of Virtual Power Purchase Agreements and the launch of a pilot Contract for Difference product indicate greater use of market-based mechanisms. It expects such products to support exchange volumes beyond the growth in overall electricity demand. “We have always assumed power exchange volume growth to be faster than power demand growth, as they keep gaining share against long term contracts. We don’t expect them to reach European levels at 50% or higher share of power traded in India, but do expect them to reach 20-25% of India’s power traded in the long term,” Bernstein said. The brokerage said the two products could help exchanges move towards a 20-25% share of electricity traded in India over the long term. This remains an important part of its medium-term volume thesis even as near-term conditions remain difficult. This results in a 4% cut to its FY27 earnings per share estimate to Rs 6.04 from Rs 6.31 earlier. Its FY28 earnings per share estimate has been raised to Rs 6.99 from Rs 5.06. Transaction charges remain the bigger long-term concern The delay in market coupling reduces the immediate pressure on Indian Energy Exchange, but Bernstein continues to see transaction charges as a key long-term concern. The brokerage referred to the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission’s April 2023 order, which directed the regulator to prepare a discussion paper on transaction charges using international benchmarks and an assessment of the risks involved in the power exchange business. Bernstein believes the regulator is likely to wait for market coupling to take effect before deciding on transaction charges. That lowers the immediate risk of a cut, although the brokerage still expects charges to come down over time. “We continue to see the current transaction charges as unsustainable, especially with power prices falling in India, and expect it to come down eventually. However, the near term risk is lower as we believe the regulator is likely to wait for market coupling to be executed before taking a call on transaction charges,” Bernstein said. The brokerage also compared Indian Energy Exchange’s transaction charges with those of European power exchanges. Its analysis showed the exchange charging about 4 paise per kilowatt-hour, compared with around 1 paise at EEX and 0.6 paise at Nord Pool. Bernstein said higher trading volumes at European exchanges partly explain the difference, but expects Indian Energy Exchange’s charge to decline as volumes grow. docs.title: A Rs 9,000 cr stock controls Rs 59,500 cr of Britannia. Another trades at 12x
docs.text: High ROCE, Low PE, Still Ignored? Value for money stocks are easy to find. But such stocks that also earn a high return on the money put into them are much rarer. ROCE, or return on capital employed, shows the profit a company makes on every Rs 100 of capital it uses. PE, or price-to-earnings, shows what the market pays for every rupee of profit. I ran a screen for profit-making companies with a high ROCE and a low PE this week. Two smallcap names stood out, and each hides in the shadow of a far more famous one. The first is the 163-year-old Wadia Group flagship that controls Britannia. The second is a Kolkata company whose clients have included cable makers such as KEI, Havells and Apar. Both earn a ROCE above 30%. Both trade at a PE much lower than their respective industry medians. A low PE rarely comes without a reason. The real question is whether that reason still holds. Let us dive in. #1 Bombay Burmah: The Rs 9,000 Crore Stock Sitting on Rs 59,500 Crore of Britannia Incorporated in 1863, The Bombay Burmah Trading Corporation began life trading teak in Burma and moved into tea estates in South India in 1913. It is the Wadia Group's flagship. With a market cap of Rs 8,966 cr, it runs tea and coffee estates and makes auto electric parts and dental products. It also holds the group's crown jewel: majority control of Britannia Industries, the maker of Good Day and Marie Gold biscuits. The Britannia Maths the Market Keeps Ignoring Britannia's shareholding filing for the June 2026 quarter shows its promoter group holding 50.55% of the company. Almost all of that block sits with step-down subsidiaries of Bombay Burmah. At Britannia's market value of about Rs 1,15,858 cr, that stake is worth over Rs 59,000 cr on paper. Bombay Burmah's own market value is about 15% of that figure. Put simply, each Bombay Burmah share carries close to Rs 8,500 worth of Britannia stock, and trades at about Rs 1,300. FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now There are reasons for the gap. The stake is not for sale, so shareholders only see its value through dividends passed up the chain. That is why Indian holding companies almost always trade at a discount. The group also carries the scar of Go First, the airline in which Bombay Burmah held about a third. When the airline collapsed in 2023, the company made provisions of Rs 1,866 cr, and FY23 ended in a consolidated loss of Rs 534 cr. Half the Profit Belongs to Britannia's Other Shareholders Financial YearFY21FY22FY23FY24FY25FY265-Yr CAGRSales (Rs Cr)13,39614,50716,62317,10918,29819,5398%EBITDA (Rs Cr)2,1501,5951,7262,8673,1363,43210%Net Profit (Rs Cr)1,278809-5341,6892,1992,49914% Source: Screener.in (Consolidated) EBITDA is operating profit before other income. Net profit includes the share of minority shareholders. Read the net profit row with care. It includes the part of Britannia's profit that belongs to Britannia's other shareholders, which is close to half. In the June 2026 quarter, consolidated profit was Rs 582.67 cr. Profit belonging to Bombay Burmah's own shareholders was Rs 288.16 cr, up about 20% on the year, as per results filed with BSE. On that owners' measure, earnings per share rose from Rs 52.96 in FY21 to Rs 178.10 in FY26, a compound rate of about 27%. The balance sheet has cleaned up too. Borrowings fell from Rs 6,542 cr in FY23 to Rs 1,590 cr in FY26. ROCE stands at 33%, with a return on equity (ROE) of about 19%. The Rs 249 Crore Block Deal On 18th September 2026, 18.34 lakh shares, or 2.62% of the company, changed hands in a block deal at about Rs 1,360 apiece. The stock jumped nearly 10% as traders guessed at a big new buyer. Filings with BSE a few days later told a quieter story. The seller was Nusli Wadia, whose stake fell from 10% to 7.37%. The buyer was Nowrosjee Wadia and Sons, a promoter group company, which now holds 44.57%. It was an inter-se transfer, shares moving from one family pocket to another. The promoter group's total holding stayed at about 74%. By 6th October, the stock had slipped to a fresh 52-week low. ALSO READ5 investment themes, 20 stocks: How to ride India’s next capex boom Valuation: 7x Earnings, and Flat for Five Years The share price of Bombay Burmah was around Rs 1,152 in October 2021 and as on 7th October 2026 it was Rs 1,285. That is a small gain in five years, and the stock is trading about 40% below its 52-week high of Rs 2,135. As for valuations, the stock trades at a PE of about 7x, while the current industry median is 44x. The 10-year median PE of the company is 16x, while the industry median for the same period is 47x. Note that the company's PE history is bent out of shape by FY22 and FY23, when airline losses crushed earnings. If Britannia, itself near a 52-week low, recovers, or the group simplifies its structure, the gap could narrow. If not, cheap can stay cheap for years. docs.title: Airtel tariff hike: Postpaid plans costlier by Rs 50, prepaid increase may follow
docs.text: Bharti Airtel raised postpaid plan prices by Rs 50 a month from October 8, taking tariffs up by about 3% to 11% across plans. The company has also added free roaming for one international trip a year to the new plans, according to a Motilal Oswal Financial Services report. Airtel postpaid plan prices The individual postpaid plan now costs Rs 499 a month, up from Rs 449. A family plan for two moved from Rs 699 to Rs 749. The family plan for three rose from Rs 999 to Rs 1,049. Plans for four members went up from Rs 1,199 to Rs 1,249 and from Rs 1,399 to Rs 1,449. The family plan for five now costs Rs 1,799 against Rs 1,749 earlier, as per the report. The free international roaming offer matches a similar one recently introduced by Vodafone Idea. International roaming packs otherwise start at Rs 999, the report noted. ALSO READMuthoot Microfin Q2 Update: Collection efficiency climbs to 98.11%; AUM hits Rs 15,323 cr Airtel postpaid ARPU and subscribers Postpaid users made up about 8% of Bharti Airtel's subscriber mix as of June 2026. The segment had around 30 million paying subscribers. It brought in an estimated Rs 3,500 crore in revenue, or nearly 12% of the company's wireless revenue, according to the report. Average revenue per user (ARPU) in postpaid was estimated at Rs 395 a month. The overall figure for the company was Rs 264. The postpaid base has grown 12% to 13% a year for several quarters. Prepaid subscribers grew about 3% a year, the report said. Postpaid customers also tend to stay longer. They have more flexibility on data use, content bundles and family plans, the brokerage noted. Airtel tariff hike impact on ARPU Motilal Oswal estimated that the price hike could lift blended ARPU by about 1%. Free international roaming would offset part of that gain, the report said. The brokerage had already assumed a Rs 50 hike in postpaid plans from December 2026. It had also built in a 15% hike in prepaid smartphone tariffs in the same month. The earlier postpaid move therefore did not lead to major changes in its near-term estimates, according to the report. The increase could still help Bharti Airtel offset any ARPU dilution from voice-only packs with 28 to 30 days of validity, if these are launched, the report added. Airtel tariff hike history The brokerage pointed to earlier tariff cycles. In 2019 and 2021, changes to postpaid plans came about six to nine months before prepaid hikes, as per the report. In May 2019, Bharti Airtel dropped its entry-level Rs 299 postpaid plan. A prepaid hike followed in November and December that year. In July 2021, the company changed its family postpaid plans and raised the price of add-on SIMs by Rs 50. It also lifted entry-level corporate postpaid plans from Rs 199 to Rs 299. A prepaid hike again followed in November and December, according to the report. The report said Bharti Airtel had used postpaid as a testing ground in the past. The company leads the postpaid segment, and Reliance Jio does not have a meaningful presence there. That allowed it to gauge customer and competitor reactions before touching prepaid prices. The 2024 cycle, led by Jio, was different. Prepaid and postpaid prices were revised together, the report noted. ALSO READIT sector Q2FY27: Infosys, HCL Tech, Wipro, Tech Mahindra results, interim dividend dates Prepaid tariff hike outlook Motilal Oswal expected prepaid hikes to follow within six months and said broader industry tariff increases could come soon. It also pointed to Bharti Airtel's recent removal of the Rs 299 entry-level prepaid data plan. Together with the postpaid hike, this should help the company keep its lead over peers in ARPU growth, according to the report. The brokerage retained its Buy rating on Bharti Airtel with a target price of Rs 2,250. It said the risk-reward for the stock was attractive.

docs.title: Rs 18,000 to Rs 4.2 lakh a month: How this 26-year-old made Rs 75 lakh in 3 years
docs.text: Over the past few months, we have written about people who took very different routes to building wealth. Some started with modest salaries and built sizeable assets over decades. Others reached high incomes early and used aggressive saving and investing to accelerate their journey. There have also been stories of people who faced a sudden loss of income and had to rebuild their finances from scratch. Bengaluru-based Arjun Parmar's journey is different. The 26-year-old started working in 2023 with a salary of just around Rs 18,000 a month. Three years later, his CTC was Rs 4.2 lakh per month, translating to an annual CTC of over Rs 50 lakh. The journey, however, was anything but smooth. He started with a non-circuital engineering branch, struggled to get a technology job through campus placements, spent his early working years keeping expenses low, got a major salary jump and then lost his high-paying job within a year. Today, he has financial assets of around Rs 65-75 lakh, owns a house in his hometown of Ujjain and is targeting a Rs 5 crore investment corpus by the age of 35. For Arjun, the biggest lesson from the journey is simple: a high salary can accelerate wealth creation, but only if you don't allow your lifestyle to rise at the same speed. ALSO READNo Stocks. No Mutual Funds. No Crypto. Yet He's Set to Retire at 50 With Over Rs 3 Crore From a modest home in Ujjain to an NIT Arjun grew up in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh, in a modest middle-class family. His father, Rajesh Parmar, 56, still runs a small electrical goods trading business. His mother, Sunita Parmar, 52, is a homemaker. His younger sister Riya, 22, is pursuing her master's degree from a Bhopal college. There was no large family investment portfolio or inherited wealth waiting for him. His parents' biggest financial priority was his education. Arjun studied in an English-medium school in Ujjain and was particularly interested in mathematics and science. He appeared for JEE in 2019 and secured admission to an NIT. But college did not go exactly as he had planned. He wanted a computer science-related branch but ended up studying Mechanical Engineering. The problem became more obvious during placements. Several technology companies did not allow students from non-circuital branches to apply for software roles. While some of his friends started getting placed, Arjun found himself watching from the sidelines. Then came the Covid pandemic. Instead of spending the entire period worrying about his branch, he started learning programming. He began working on data structures, algorithms and software development and spent several hours a day solving coding problems. That decision eventually changed the direction of his career. First salary: Rs 18,000 a month Arjun graduated in 2023 and joined Tech Mahindra in July that year as a software trainee His annual compensation was around Rs 2.2 lakh, with his monthly take-home at roughly Rs 18,000. For someone who had spent four years studying engineering, it was not the start he had imagined. Some of his college friends were earning several times that amount. But instead of waiting for the next big opportunity, he started with what he had. He sent around Rs 5,000-7,000 a month to his parents and tried to save whatever remained. Towards the end of 2023, he also started his first SIP. It was only Rs 5,000 a month in an index fund. The amount was small. But it established a habit that would become important later. Arjun says his first year at work taught him something that he still follows today: increasing income can have a much bigger impact on wealth creation than trying to squeeze out a few extra percentage points from investments. First big switch: Rs 18,000 to Rs 1 lakh a month The first major change came in October 2024. After around 15 months at Tech Mahindra, Parmar switched to Accenture and his compensation jumped to around Rs 12 lakh a year. The move also took him from Ujjain to Bengaluru. For the first time, he was earning around Rs 1 lakh a month before deductions. But Bengaluru also brought higher expenses. Arjun initially shared an apartment with colleagues and kept his monthly expenses below Rs 45,000. He relied heavily on BMTC buses and the Metro and avoided cabs unless necessary. His salary had increased sharply, but his lifestyle had not increased at the same pace. But this gave him room to increase his investments and his SIPs went up to around Rs 35,000-40,000 a month. He also increased the amount he sent home to around Rs 15,000 a month. By March 2025, after roughly 20 months of working, he had accumulated around Rs 8-10 lakh across savings, EPF and investments. That was still a modest amount compared with what he would accumulate later. But it was the beginning of the snowball. Then came the salary jump In August 2025, Arjun cracked a job at another large global technology company in the FAANG+ category. His CTC jumped to around Rs 45 lakh, including fixed salary, bonus and RSUs. He was 25. For someone who had started at Rs 18,000 a month, the jump was enormous, and for the first time, lifestyle inflation became a real temptation. He moved into better accommodation and also started eating out more. And also there were more gadgets, more travel and more discretionary spending. His monthly expenses briefly crossed Rs 1.2 lakh. But he did something important at the same time - increased his investments. His monthly investments rose to around Rs 1 lakh-1.25 lakh. His core portfolio consisted of index funds, flexi-cap funds and some mid-cap exposure and he also started buying a few direct stocks. But, he was not trying to become a trader. The idea was simple: use a high income to accumulate long-term assets. docs.title: Only 1 public charger for every 235 EVs: 2 stocks taking on India’s EV bottleneck
docs.text: The electric vehicle (EV) story in India is no longer only about how many EVs are being sold. It is also about what happens after the vehicle leaves the showroom. Where will it charge? And is India building enough charging infrastructure to keep pace with EV adoption? The numbers suggest that the gap is still wide. Electric Vehicle registrations reached 24.5 lakh units in FY26, up 26% from 19.5 lakh in FY25, taking EVs to 8.7% of total vehicle sales. At the same time, public charging stations crossed 29,000 by December 2025. The government has also earmarked ₹2,000 crore under the PM E-DRIVE scheme to support charging infrastructure. But the charging network is growing from a relatively small base. CareEdge Research estimates that public EV charging stations increased from 5,151 in CY2022 to 26,367 by April 2025. Even after this expansion, India had only around one public charger for every 235 EVs, leaving considerable room for the network to grow. FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now That gap is beginning to shape a new part of the EV investment story. As more electric vehicles enter the country’s roads, the demand for EV chargers is also expected to be strong. Against this backdrop, this article outlines two leading EV charging companies at the forefront of this market. #1 Tata Power: India’s EV charging network at scale Tata Power, part of the Tata Group, operates India's largest EV charging network under its Tata Power EZ Charge brand. The company covers public, bus, home, and highway locations across India. The company has one of the largest charging networks in India. Inside Tata’s 7,200-Plug Network As of Q1FY27, the company had 5,970 public charging points across 717 cities and towns. By the end of FY27, the company plans to expand its electric bus network to 1,258 charging points. Overall, the company has 7,200 charging points. Additionally, Tata Power's total residential installations increased to 246,065 home chargers. To help drivers with long-distance trips, it also installed over 1,160 fast chargers on 254 highway corridors. Last year, in 2025, Tata Power also formed a partnership with Tata Passenger Electric Mobility. The venture launched its first co-branded charging hub near Terminal 2 of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport in Mumbai. This facility runs entirely on renewable energy. App Drives 65% Revenue Surge Tata Power EZ Charge mobile application has 5.6 lakh registered users in FY26. During FY26, the platform recorded 30.2 lakh charging sessions and delivered 2596.4 lakh units of electricity. The electric vehicle charging division generated ₹192 crore in operational revenue during FY26. Public charging revenue specifically grew by 65% during FY26. ALSO READ41% revenue growth, 30.8% ROCE: This Tata-backed smallcap could be a backdoor EV play 2030 Target: Tier II Expansion Looking ahead, the company aims to install over 10,000 public charging points nationwide by 2030. Home charger installations are projected to reach over 7.5 lakh units by 2030. This aligns with the government’s objective of reaching 30% electric vehicle adoption across India by 2030. Tata Power plans to expand charging points deeper into Tier II and Tier III cities and towns. Management states that the installation of fast chargers will continue to grow along major highway stretches. This would help address driver range anxiety during long-distance travel. The focus would be on charging setups for electric buses, workplaces, and residential complexes. Q1FY27: Net Profit Jumps 11% Financially, the company reported an 8.2% year-over-year increase in revenue to ₹17,464 crore in Q1FY27. EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortisation) increased 8.1% to ₹4,249 crore, while margin stood at 24.3%. Consequently, net profit increased 11% to ₹1,410 crore. Tata Power Share Price #2 Exicom Tele-Systems: Building the hardware behind India’s EV charging growth Exicom Tele-Systems operates across two main business segments: EV Charger Business and Critical Power Business. In the EV Charger business, the company provides hardware, software and integrated charging solutions for passenger vehicles, commercial fleets and public networks. Exicom is a major player in India's electric mobility infrastructure. The company has sold over 215,000 EV chargers globally. Consolidated revenue from the EV charger business grew 49.7% year-over-year to ₹153.9 crore in Q1FY27. Management stated that internal volume momentum continues to grow. The business now accounts for 46.5% of revenue. Inside the ₹1,400-Cr Order Book The company's order book stood at ₹200+ crore as of June 2026, which includes direct export orders worth ₹16.5-17 crore. The total consolidated order book reached a record ₹1,400+ crore across the EV charger business and Critical Power. The company acquired a 100% business share for 7.4 kW home wallbox chargers with a leading passenger 4W OEM. Exicom also launched a special Type-7 charger for a large 7W OEM. The company also renewed and expanded its supply agreement with a large commercial truck OEM. Notably, the company holds a 50% market share in India’s passenger vehicle wallbox charger segment. Hyderabad Ramp & 10-Nation Push In Q1 FY27, Exicom added 15 new charge point operator (CPO) network accounts. For this, it has confirmed orders for 180+ DC chargers to be delivered by October 2026. Existing CPOs have placed repeat orders worth over ₹50 crore. The company also launched new products during the quarter. The company is also commissioning new production lines in Hyderabad and has increased its monthly volume capacity for AC chargers. Management expects the run rate to increase by another 50% in three months. docs.title: 7 reasons why the market is falling today: Nifty below 22,300, Sensex slides over 1,000 points
docs.text: The stock market selloff has deepened through today's trading session. What started as a weak opening turned into a sharper fall by afternoon trade. The Sensex plunged more than 1,000 points to slip below 71,700, hitting an intraday low of 71,691.95. The Nifty also fell more than 300 points, or 1.37%, to trade below 22,300. But what is driving the sudden pressure on equities? Rising crude oil prices, a weaker rupee, foreign selling and concerns over higher interest rates are coming together at the same time. Here are seven factors investors are watching. #1 Crude oil crosses $103 Oil has emerged as one of the biggest concerns for Indian markets. Brent crude prices rose over 3.5% to cross $103 per barrel as investors worried about supply disruptions from the Middle East. Attacks on shipping in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz have added to concerns over global supplies. Higher crude prices can also increase India’s import bill and put pressure on inflation. ALSO READBeyond warships: 2 stocks riding India’s Rs 69,725 cr small-shipbuilding push Sunny Agrawal, Head - Fundamental Research at SBI Securities, said, “Spike in crude oil prices to $103 per barrel, weakness in USDINR, profit-taking in stocks that were in a strong uptrend, and persistent aggressive FII outflows are the key factors weighing on the market”. #2 RBI turns more hawkish The Reserve Bank of India’s latest policy decision has also changed the market mood. The central bank raised the repo rate by 25 basis points, marking its first rate hike in nearly four years. More importantly, the Monetary Policy Committee shifted its stance from ‘neutral’ to ‘calibrated tightening’. That signals that rates could remain higher for longer. #3 Bond yields climbs The global bond selloff has added another layer of pressure. The US 30-year bond yield climbed above 5.7%, while the 10-year yield moved above 5.3%. #4 Foreign investors keep selling Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) have remained aggressive sellers of Indian equities. Persistent selling by overseas investors has put pressure on large-cap stocks. Dr. V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments, said, “With the US 10-year bond yield hovering above 5.3%, FIIs will continue to sell on every rally. This will put the Nifty large-caps under pressure for some more time.” #5 Profit booking hits recent winners Stocks that had seen strong upward moves are now facing profit-taking. Agrawal also pointed to “profit-taking in stocks that were in a strong uptrend” as one of the factors behind the decline. #6 Heavyweights drag the indices ITC, Adani Ports, InterGlobe Aviation (IndiGo), Power Grid Corporation of India and Reliance Industries led losses, declining up to 4%. On the other side, Titan and major Information Technology stocks such as Tech Mahindra, HCL Technologies, Tata Consultancy Services and Infosys gained up to 2%. ALSO READ6 ‘Buy’ recommendations by Jefferies, with 44% to 56% upside potential #7 Broader market selling intensifies The Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 100 indices fell as much as 2%. Nifty Metal dropped around 3%, while Nifty Realty and Nifty Oil & Gas declined around 2%. What investors need to watch Higher rates, expensive crude and continued FII selling are keeping pressure on valuations. Vijayakumar said, “A reversal in this trend will happen only when FIIs turn buyers, and there is no clarity on when this will happen.” He added, “In brief, this frustrating period in the market might continue for some more time. Remaining invested in value stocks will be rewarded in the long run. Investors should also look at the good opportunities in fixed income in this rising rate environment.”
